articles.title: Apuestas y pronósticos España vs Croacia
articles.standfirst: 1XBET te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a España y Croacia en el Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán correspondiente a la jornada 2 del Grupo 3 de la Liga A de la Nations League
articles.summary: 1XBET te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a España y Croacia en el Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán correspondiente a la jornada 2 del Grupo 3 de la Liga A de la Nations League
articles.body: España afronta su segundo compromiso de esta Nations League después de protagonizar un estreno de máxima exigencia en Wembley. La selección española consiguió remontar ante Inglaterra para comenzar la competición con una prestigiosa victoria a domicilio, prolongando así la buena dinámica del combinado nacional después de ganar el Mundial. Ahora, buscará mantener ese ritmo ante su afición en un duelo que puede servir para consolidar el liderato del grupo en solitario. Favorito para el partido entre España y Croacia Croacia también llega a esta segunda jornada después de sumar los tres puntos en su estreno. El combinado balcánico derrotó a la República Checa de Santi Denia en un encuentro en el que, además, Luka Modric volvió a dejar su sello en forma de gol. Pese al buen inicio croata, las casas de apuestas conceden un favoritismo muy marcado a España: 1XBET ofrece una cuota de 1.17 por la victoria española, 7.30 por el empate y 15.00 por el triunfo de Croacia. Ambos equipos marcan El mercado de ambos equipos marcan presenta una tendencia idéntica en los dos combinados y aparece como una opción a tener en cuenta en las apuestas deportivas. España cumplió este pronóstico en su remontada ante Inglaterra, en un encuentro en el que recibió un gol pero terminó imponiéndose. Croacia también vio marcar a ambos equipos en su victoria frente a la República Checa, por lo que sus respectivos estrenos dejaron un escenario favorable para este mercado. 1XBET ofrece una cuota de 2.14 por el 'sí' y de 1.64 por el 'no'. Número total de goles (Over/Under) La línea de goles también parte de una estadística coincidente entre ambas selecciones. En la victoria de España contra Inglaterra se superaron los 2.5 goles totales, mientras que en el triunfo de Croacia frente a la República Checa también se alcanzó esta barrera. Los dos combinados demostraron capacidad para participar en encuentros con marcadores elevados en su estreno, aunque ahora se medirán en un duelo de mayor exigencia. 1XBET paga a 1.45 que se superen los 2.5 goles y a 2.53 que se registren menos de 2.5 tantos. Goles en ambas mitades El mercado de goles en ambas mitades presenta diferencias entre los dos equipos después de sus respectivos debuts. España cumplió este pronóstico ante Inglaterra, ya que hubo goles tanto antes como después del descanso durante su remontada en Wembley. Croacia, en cambio, no lo hizo frente a la República Checa, puesto que todos los tantos del encuentro llegaron durante la segunda parte. 1XBET ofrece una cuota de 1.44 por que haya gol en ambas mitades y de 2.57 por que no se produzca este escenario.

articles.title: El espectacular arranque del Castellón todavía no convence
articles.standfirst: Tonybet sigue dando al Girona como principal favorito al ascenso
articles.summary: Tonybet sigue dando al Girona como principal favorito al ascenso
articles.body: LaLiga Hypermotion no se detiene por el parón de selecciones y ya ha completado las siete primeras jornadas con una sorpresa mayúscula en lo más alto de la clasificación. El Castellón marcha como líder después de mantenerse invicto y sumar 19 de los 21 puntos posibles tras su victoria frente al Leganés. Un arranque espectacular que no se veía en la categoría desde el Elche de la temporada 2012-13 y que ha colocado al conjunto castellonense como el gran protagonista de este inicio de campeonato. Aquel Elche terminó ascendiendo a Primera División... pero el precedente todavía no es suficiente para convencer en las apuestas deportivas. Tonybet asigna al Castellón una cuota de 6.01 para lograr el ascenso. Exactamente, la misma que al Almería, tercero con 15 puntos después de imponerse al Mallorca. El conjunto balear, que empieza a perder posiciones en la carrera por el ascenso, se sitúa bastante más lejos con una cuota de 9.02. La clasificación dice una cosa y los pronósticos, por ahora, otra bien distinta. El favorito para regresar a Primera sigue siendo el Girona... a pesar de ocupar la quinta posición con 13 puntos después de derrotar al Albacete en Montilivi. Tonybet le otorga una cuota de 5.51 para regresar a Primera, mientras que el Eibar se acerca peligrosamente por detrás del líder. Los armeros vienen de imponerse a Las Palmas y ya sólo están a un punto del Castellón. Sin embargo, su cuota para ascender se eleva hasta los 7.02. Las mejores casas de apuestas siguen confiando así más en la trayectoria y el potencial de determinados equipos que en el espectacular arranque de los castellonenses. También marcha a un ritmo frenético el Burgos, sexto de este grupo de equipos que ahora mismo ocupa las posiciones de privilegio. El conjunto burgalés suma tres victorias consecutivas y acumula ya cinco jornadas sin perder, aunque esa dinámica todavía no ha provocado un gran cambio en los pronósticos. Tonybet sitúa su cuota de ascenso en 21.06, muy alejada de la de los principales candidatos. Una muestra más de que queda muchísimo campeonato por delante y de que siete jornadas todavía no parecen suficientes para modificar las jerarquías establecidas antes del inicio de la temporada. Aún queda mucha tela que cortar hasta llegar a la jornada 42. El Castellón ha puesto la Hypermotion patas arriba, pero la carrera por el ascenso está lejos de reducirse a un solo protagonista. De hecho, a los seis equipos que actualmente ocupan las posiciones de 'playoff' les separan, únicamente, seis puntos. Un margen mínimo que permite pensar que la clasificación puede cambiar por completo en cuestión de semanas... y que el espectacular inicio del Castellón todavía tendrá que resistir muchas curvas antes de convertirse en una candidatura real al ascenso. articles.title: 'Feels like a dream': An Se-young completes badminton's golden sweep with Asian Games triumph over Akane Yamaguchi
articles.summary: An Se-young added another glittering chapter to her extraordinary career on Tuesday, defeating Japan’s three-time world champion Akane Yamaguchi 21-17,
articles.body: An Se-young added another glittering chapter to her extraordinary career on Tuesday, defeating Japan’s three-time world champion Akane Yamaguchi 21-17, 21-9 to win Asian Games gold and underline her status as the world’s No. 1-ranked female badminton player.The South Korean star has now collected virtually every major prize the sport has to offer. Already a Paris Olympic champion and two-time world champion, An has added a second Asian Games gold medal to her collection, further strengthening her extraordinary claim to the top of the women’s game.An dropped to her knees after sealing victory, before arching backwards and looking skyward in an emotional celebration.“It feels like a dream,” An said. “I am so happy and I'm overwhelmed with emotion as I think back to all the hard work I've put in.”Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleAn leaves Yamaguchi chasing shadowsThe final was a demonstration of An’s athleticism, court coverage and relentless pressure. She repeatedly used the full width and depth of the court, forcing Yamaguchi into long, exhausting movements before finding openings to finish points.“I decided to approach the match with the aim of making my opponent feel rushed and forcing her to move around a lot,” An said.Yamaguchi, a three-time world champion, struggled to match An’s pace in the second game as the South Korean surged away to a commanding 21-9 victory.An had earlier defeated China’s Chen Yufei in the semifinals, extending her winning streak against her Chinese rival to five matches.From controversy to another major titleAn’s journey to the top has also included difficult moments. After winning Olympic gold in Paris, she criticised South Korea’s national training system, saying she had been forced to play through a knee injury and questioning some training methods. She later backed away from her threat to pursue an independent path.But on the court, An’s response has been emphatic. articles.title: Asian Games 2026 Medal Tally: How two gold medals lifted India back into the top 10
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India’s Asian Games campaign received a significant boost on Tuesday as two gold medals on Day 10 helped the country climb back into the top 10
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s Asian Games campaign received a significant boost on Tuesday as two gold medals on Day 10 helped the country climb back into the top 10 of the medal table. India won eight medals overall, taking its tally to 53 — six gold, 21 silver and 26 bronze — to move into 10th position.The two gold medals came in shooting and athletics, with Neeru Dhanda producing a historic performance in the women’s trap individual event before the Indian women’s 4x400m relay team delivered another top finish.The gold-medal double also ended India’s wait for the top step of the podium after two days without a gold, following the double triumph in kabaddi on September 26.Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleNeeru, women’s relay team deliver golden doubleDhanda made history by winning India’s first-ever Asian Games gold in the women’s trap event. Despite incessant rain affecting visibility, she remained composed to finish with 28 hits in the final, setting an Asian Games record. It was also India’s first individual shooting gold of the Games.Athletics then produced another gold as Kiran, Prachi Choudhary, MR Poovamma and Vithya Ramraj won the women’s 4x400m relay in 3:29.69.For Poovamma, the 36-year-old, it was another chapter in her Asian Games career after being part of India’s gold-medal winning relay teams in 2014 and 2018. Vithya added the relay gold to her breakthrough campaign after earlier bettering PT Usha’s more than four-decade-old national record in the 400m hurdles.Eight medals but mixed athletics resultsIndia’s athletics campaign produced a mixed bag, with 19-year-old Pooja Singh winning high jump bronze after clearing 1.84m and Gulveer Singh completing a medal treble with bronze in the 5000m, adding to his silver medals in the 10,000m and 1500m.India also won bronze in the 4x100m mixed relay through Gurindervir Singh, Sneha Sathyanarayana, Animesh Kujur and Harita Bhadra in a season-best 41.06 seconds.The men’s 4x400m relay team of Vishal TK, Dharamveer Choudhary, Jay Kumar and T Manu settled for bronze in 3:01.61, missing out on defending the Hangzhou title.Shooting added another silver in the women’s trap team event, while boxing guaranteed three medals. Narender took bronze after losing his 90+kg semifinal, while Parveen and Ankush Panghal advanced to their respective finals.Two golds lift India back into top 10The twin gold-medal haul proved crucial in the overall standings. India’s 53 medals moved the country back into 10th place, while China continued to dominate with 254 medals.Japan followed with 183 medals, while South Korea and Uzbekistan had 95 and 44 respectively.For India, the biggest takeaway from Day 10 was the return to the top 10, powered by two gold medals that took its overall haul beyond the 50-medal mark.Asian Games Medal Tally after Day 10RankNationGoldSilverBronzeTotal1China14362492542Japan4571671833South Korea242744954Uzbekistan141713445Thailand12912336Bahrain1154207Iran101611378Kazakhstan91425489North Korea7561810INDIA6212653Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: WWE Rumors on Jaida Parker, Jey Uso, Naomi's Return, Dennis Haskins' GM Pitch Revealed
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

WWE Reportedly Alluded to Jey/Jaida Relationship Purposely

Those who are in the know were reportedly rewarded by WWE on Monday night as it relates to the interaction between Jey Uso and Jaida Parker on Raw.

At the start of the show, The Bloodline rushed toward a vehicle due to their belief that 946 was inside, but Parker stepped out instead. A shocked Jey asked her why she was there, and she responded by saying she was going to speak with Raw general manager Adam Pearce.

Jey and Jaida are a real-life couple, and while that was not explicitly stated on Raw, those who were already aware of it understood the significance of that moment.

According to Dave Meltzer of Wrestling Observer Radio (h/t H Jenkins of Ringside News), wanted to address the relationship status of Jey and Jaida in a subtle way without needing to explain it on screen.

Meltzer went on to express his belief that the nature of their relationship will not actually be discussed within the fabric of the storyline.

In Raw's closing segment, Jacob Fatu threw hands with Royce Keys before a car shockingly came speeding into frame and hit Fatu.

Parker exited the vehicle and acted horrified by what happened before revealing that it was actually part of the plan and she was the newest member of 946.

With that, Parker and Jey are now on opposing sides in WWE's most personal rivalry despite their status as a real-life couple.

WWE Reportedly Preparing for Naomi to Return Soon

After being out of action for more than a year, Naomi reportedly may be on the verge of returning to WWE programming.

False Finish reported that WWE is "currently preparing" for Naomi to return "in the near future."

That report came just minutes after the shocking end to Raw, which saw Parker hit Fatu with her car and join 946.

With 946 now having a women's Superstar in the group, it would make sense for The Bloodline to counter with a women's wrestler of their own, and Naomi would undoubtedly fit the bill.

Naomi is the wife of Bloodline member Jimmy Uso, and she is a hugely accomplished WWE veteran who has held three women's world titles and two women's tag team titles.

In August 2025, Naomi announced that she had to step away from WWE because she was pregnant with her first child.

At the time, Naomi was the women's world champion, as she successfully cashed in the Money in the Bank contract during a match between Rhea Ripley and Iyo Sky at Evolution.

Naomi beat Ripley and Sky in a Triple Threat rematch at SummerSlam, and that turned out to be the final match before her hiatus.

If and when she returns, Naomi could add a new dimension to The Bloodline and allow them to cancel out Parker's presence in 946.

WWE Reportedly Once Offered Haskins GM Role

WWE reportedly once made actor Dennis Haskins an offer to serve in an on-screen authority role.

According to Meltzer (h/t Steve Carrier of Ringside News), WWE wanted Haskins to serve as general manager, but Haskins declined the opportunity because of the amount of travel it would have entailed.

Haskins, who died Monday at the age of 75, is best known for playing the principal Mr. Belding in the hugely popular 1990s television series Saved by the Bell .

He was also recognized as a huge professional wrestling fan who made multiple appearances on WWE-related programming.

Haskins was notably featured on The JBL & Cole Show and Zack Ryder's Z! True Long Island Story .

From the late 2000s to the late 2010s, WWE cycled through many on-screen authority figures as the general managers on Raw and SmackDown.

Most of them were from the wrestling world, whereas Haskins could have used his legitimate acting skills to put a different spin on the role.

Although it never came to fruition, WWE's reported interest in hiring Haskins at one time is proof of his popularity and the respect he garnered for his performances.

articles.title: Wild's Brock Faber Has Surgery for Fractured Skull, Latest Injury Updates and Timeline to Return
articles.summary: The Minnesota Wild announced on Tuesday that defenseman Brock Faber underwent successful surgery after suffering a fractured skull.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Wild announced on Tuesday that defenseman Brock Faber underwent successful surgery after suffering a fractured skull.

Faber suffered the injury in Friday's preseason game against the Dallas Stars and had surgery on Sunday. A timeline for his return will be provided at a later date.

Per TSN , Faber took a puck off the left side of his head in the second period of Friday's game. He skated to the bench under his own power before returning to the ice and playing the rest of the period, but he was held out of the third.

A five-year veteran, Faber is coming off his best season, as he finished the 2025-26 campaign with career highs of 15 goals and 51 points. He averaged 24:41 of ice time during the regular season and increased to 29:44 in the playoffs as the Wild advanced to the second round before losing to the Colorado Avalanche in five games. In addition to his continued rise in the NHL, Faber has also established himself at the international level. He was a member of the Team USA squad that brought home the gold medal at the 2026 Milano Cortina Winter Olympics. He also helped Team USA earn silver at the 4 Nations Face-Off.

articles.title: Why Athletics Outfielder Zack Gelof Is Suing Tigers For Damages
articles.summary: Athletics outfielder Zack Gelof has filed a lawsuit against the Tigers for damages after his right knee slammed into a Comerica Park fence.
articles.body: Athletics outfielder Zack Gelof has filed a lawsuit against the Detroit Tigers, Ilitch Holdings and the Detroit-Wayne County Stadium Authority for damages after his right knee slammed into a Comerica Park fence during a game last summer. "We are aware of the lawsuit and do not comment on pending litigation," the Tigers said in a statement on Tuesday. Gelof was hurt in the third inning of a 4-1 loss to the Tigers on July 9 while making a sliding catch in foul territory and colliding with a metal fence. The 26-year-old infielder immediately grabbed his knee in obvious pain, a tear in his uniform pants showed where his leg made contact with the fence. He was left with a deep cut under his right knee cap, just missing the tendon, and didn’t play again until Aug. 10. "This injury could have easily been prevented through the most basic and inexpensive design," said Gelof’s attorney, Jon Marko. "It doesn’t take a stadium design expert to realize that sharp metal fencing in an area where players are required to slide and play around is a recipe for disaster like the one that occurred here. "All they had to do was put cheap padding up like they did after Zack was injured and this entire incident could have been avoided. My son’s little league diamond is safer." Gelof hit .256 with 22 homers and 55 RBIs — both career highs — in 111 games during his fourth season. The A's finished the season 64-98, putting them ahead of only the Los Angeles and the Colorado Rockies in the majors. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Same Faces, New Places: How College Football's Transfer QBs Are Making An Impact
articles.summary: FOX Sports' Brady Quinn breaks down transfer quarterbacks Darian Mensah, Sam Leavitt and Dylan Raiola and highlights the QBs and matchups to watch.
articles.body: Welcome to "In The Pocket" — my opportunity to take you on a tour around college football and highlight the quarterbacks driving the conversation across the sport. This week, I’m taking a look at some of the quarterbacks who are back for another season of college football, but wearing different uniforms: same faces, new places. These are signal-callers who have already proven they can play at this level, and now they’re making an impact at their new schools. Whether you like it or not, the transfer portal is here to stay. But some of the sport’s top signal-callers are proving that sometimes, a fresh start is exactly what a quarterback needs. Same Faces, New Places Darian Mensah, Miami (FL) The former Tulane and Duke signal-caller left Durham, North Carolina, for greener pastures in sunny Miami this spring. Former Hurricanes quarterback Carson Beck — also a transfer. Notice a trend here? — exhausted his college eligibility, which left a void in the team's QB room. My guess is it wasn't just about the money for Mensah, but also the opportunity to showcase his skills for a blue-blood program that gave him the best chance to win a national championship. Oh, and by the way, it doesn't hurt to have one of the best wide receivers in the nation to throw the ball to in Malachi Toney. The two have already developed a chemistry that would even make 2 Live Crew jealous. Mensah's physical gifts allow him to be a dual-threat quarterback, but he often resists the temptation to scramble, only doing so when necessary. What makes him a true game-changer is his lethal accuracy from the pocket. If there was a component missing from Miami's offense last season, it was the quarterback's ability to extend plays. That's quite the opposite with Mensah. He's a smooth operator under pressure. Mensah provides offensive coordinator Shannon Dawson with a veteran presence and the command to utilize the entirety of his playbook. One of the most ridiculous stats to showcase through four weeks of the season is that Mensah currently has more touchdown passes (14) than incompletions (12), and he has yet to throw an interception. Another notable stat: Mensah has now started 31 games in his collegiate career, which seems to be a theme among recent national championship-winning quarterbacks — Michigan's J.J. McCarthy, Ohio State's Will Howard and Indiana's Fernando Mendoza. In fact, you'd have to go back to former Alabama star Mac Jones in 2020 to find a quarterback with fewer than 20 starts who won a national championship. Keep in mind, Miami has not played a ranked opponent to date, and it won't until its clash with my Fighting Irish in November. But that road win over Wake Forest is looking better with each week. Mensah has all the ability to ace the remaining tests, starting this week when the Hurricanes head to Death Valley looking to build on their 4-0 start to the season. Sam Leavitt, LSU Limited playing time and a head coaching change led Sam Leavitt to initially transfer from Michigan State back to his West Coast roots. He committed to play for Kenny Dillingham and an Arizona State team that was looking for a spark at the quarterback position. In his first year starting, Leavitt led the Sun Devils to a Big 12 championship and a College Football Playoff berth, taking the Texas Longhorns to the wire in the CFP quarterfinals. A disappointing encore, which included a foot injury that required season-ending surgery, opened the door to the Bayou. Early returns this season have been mixed. Leavitt led the Tigers to a pair of impressive wins over Clemson and Texas A&M, but he threw three picks in the team's Week 2 win over Louisiana Tech, and then went 16-of-27 for 158 yards with a touchdown and an interception in LSU's loss to Ole Miss. When Leavitt is at his best, LSU can beat anyone in the country. The question is, can Charlie Weis Jr. and Lane Kiffin unlock his full potential and get that version of Leavitt every week? A 6-foot-2, 216-pound junior with flowing locks, Leavitt looks as if he’s casting for a "Remember the Titans" reboot, playing the role of Ronnie "Sunshine" Bass. He has the ability to take off and run, creating a dilemma for defenses and leading to some incredible plays at times. The issue is that he’s often too reliant on his ability to scramble when his first read isn’t there. I’m always hesitant to be overly critical of a quarterback playing in his first year in a system. There are a lot of moving parts, not to mention he’s still developing chemistry with his receivers. The issue is, there seems to be a pattern dating back to Leavitt’s time at Arizona State. When he gets pressured or the game is moving too fast, he looks to escape the pocket instead of keeping his eyes downfield and working through his next read. This past week was a better example of the ceiling Leavitt can offer. He was efficient, took what the defense gave him, got the ball out on time and delivered it to the right read. The offensive staff clearly coached up the mistakes from the previous two weeks, when Leavitt seemed hesitant to pull the trigger. He threw with anticipation and demonstrated why so many were high on him as a transfer quarterback and as a potential NFL Draft prospect. The small things, like stepping up in the pocket and keeping his eyes downfield, allow the Tigers' offense to take shape. Leavitt's connection with Winston Watkins Jr. is evident and should only get better as the season continues. There won't be much to take away from this week's matchup with McNeese State, but it does give Leavitt another opportunity to develop a rhythm and get more comfortable in this system. Dylan Raiola, Oregon The best backup quarterback in college football has to get some love after stepping in for an injured Dante Moore at a crucial moment and leading the Ducks to a huge win in the Coliseum. The former Nebraska quarterback transferred to Oregon knowing he would back up Moore in 2026, with the idea that the Ducks would be better positioned to compete for championships and help improve his NFL draft stock after a lackluster couple of years with the Cornhuskers. At the end of the day, it may be a blessing in disguise for both. Raiola is now needed in a big way for an Oregon team with national championship aspirations after Dante Moore made the surprising decision to return for another year. Moore’s status is now in question after taking a brutal hit to the head from USC LB Desman Stephens II. Head coach Dan Lanning has stated that Moore is "doing much better" and in "recovery mode," but the Ducks are being cautious with his return. Oregon has a bye before taking on one of the surprises in the Big Ten this season: a 4-0, Top 25-ranked UCLA team. Raiola’s arm talent has never been in question. The concern was throwing off balance when it wasn’t necessary. It’s a small sample size, but it appears that the issue has been addressed, with Raiola only utilizing that ability when necessary. What makes Raiola special, besides his arm talent, is his vision downfield. He processes at a level that allows him to anticipate windows and stretch the field vertically while also knowing when to check the ball down. We may not see him for a while after this past week’s win, but when we do, the Duck won’t miss a beat. One Name To Know … Kamario Taylor, Mississippi State Mississippi State's Kamario Taylor came into the season as an under-the-radar quarterback, but that has quickly changed. The true sophomore signal-caller has led the Bulldogs to a spot in the AP Top 25 Poll for the first time since the end of the 2022 season. The Macon, Mississippi, product is the next phenom in college football, standing at 6-foot-4, 230 pounds, and blessed with the type of athleticism that makes opposing defensive coordinators sleepless at night. Somehow, his smooth release generates more RPMs than a Dodge Challenger. After a true freshman season in which he didn’t see much playing time until the final weeks, Taylor has led his team to a perfect 4-0 record this season, including road wins over Minnesota and South Carolina and a top-25 upset of Missouri last week. If that didn’t get your attention, maybe this week will. The Bulldogs host No. 7 Alabama, and Taylor will go head-to-head with another top quarterback from the 2025 recruiting class in Keelon Russell. Given the porous pass defenses on both sides, this game should have all the fireworks and splash plays that leave us clamoring for more — and NFL teams salivating while having to wait until the 2028 NFL Draft. Enjoy! What I'm Watching … Cincinnati vs. Arizona I could give you a list of games that have my attention this weekend, but one off the beaten path that deserves consideration is the surprising, undefeated Cincinnati Bearcats heading to Tucson to take on a 3-1 Arizona team that suffered a tough road loss to BYU earlier this season. Arizona may be more spoiler than contender in the Big 12 this season, but quarterback Noah Fifita is always a pleasure to watch. The four-year starter is off to another solid start, leading the Big 12 in completion percentage, tied for the lead in touchdown passes and third in passing yards. On the other side is Cincinnati transfer quarterback JC French IV, who arrived from Georgia Southern. Another quarterback who has assimilated well, French has helped fill a huge hole left behind by Brendan Sorsby. French has been the consummate pro this season. A three-year starter who has yet to throw an interception and is completing almost 75% of his passes, he has complete command of the offense. Look for some big plays downfield in this game. articles.title: Jerry Jones Blames Cowboys Coaching Staff For Week 3 Loss To Ravens
articles.summary: Cowboys owner Jerry Jones is leaving little doubt that he believes errors in game management by his coaching staff cost them a Week 2 win.
articles.body: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones is leaving little doubt that he believes errors in game management by his coaching staff in the final seconds of a 34-31 loss to the Baltimore Ravens cost his team the victory. Speaking on his radio show Tuesday, Jones was asked what explanations there were for leaving enough seconds on the clock after a tying field goal for a defensive breakdown to put the Ravens in position for the winning kick. "There is no explanation you're satisfied with. None," Jones said. "Let's be sure that we all understand that. They [coaches] don't have one that they're satisfied with. We made mistakes during that time. There's no question about it. So there is no explanation. But there's an evaluation of how not to make the same mistakes again." Trailing 31-28, the Cowboys had a first down at the Baltimore 2-yard line with 23 seconds left when Dak Prescott threw incomplete into the end zone. After a false-start penalty against tight end Luke Schoonmaker, Prescott scrambled to the Baltimore 5, and coach Brian Schottenheimer called his final timeout with 14 seconds remaining. The coach, who is also the playcaller, instructed Prescott to either throw a quick out to wide receiver George Pickens or throw the ball away, based on the amount of time left, with no ability to stop the clock. Prescott didn't wait long to choose the throwaway, and the play lasted just four seconds. There were seven seconds remaining after Brandon Aubrey's field goal, and the Dallas defense left a gap at just about the exact spot of the target line for a Baltimore field goal. Lamar Jackson completed a 27-yard pass to Zay Flowers, got the timeout called with a second to go, and Tyler Loop made the 56-yard field goal. Schottenheimer is in his second season as a head coach after 25 years as an NFL assistant. Christian Parker is a 34-year-old making his debut as a defensive coordinator. Both will be under considerable scrutiny from fans and pundits going forward, and perhaps from their own front office. "We will be better from this experience that we had with Baltimore and what happened to us at the end of the game," Jones said. "A win would have given you another way of couching it as far as having growth and enthusiasm for having won a game like that, because we did come back, and we came back in an impressive way. All of that makes us realize we really are just at the beginning of what I hope is an exciting year for us." The Cowboys (1-2) got a break in the NFC East when two-time defending champion Philadelphia lost to the Chicago Bears and backup quarterback Case Keenum on Monday night. Dallas visits the Houston Texans (0-3) Sunday. The New York Giants, who will be without quarterback Jaxson Dart for the rest of the regular season because of a knee injury, are tied with the Eagles atop the division at 2-1. "We are very much in the hunt, and I say that principally based upon the way I feel about our team, as much or more than what’s happening with the other teams," Jones said. "Philadelphia has things that they want to work on just as the Giants do, just as we do. It makes you see how health is a factor. Availability is a factor. And we're just getting started." Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Padres Name Joe Musgrove To Wild Card Roster Despite Not Pitching Since 2024
articles.summary: Veteran right-hander Joe Musgrove is on the San Diego Padres’ roster for their NL Wild Card Series nearly two full years after his most recent appearance in a major league game
articles.body: Veteran right-hander Joe Musgrove is on the San Diego Padres ' roster for their NL Wild Card Series nearly two full years after his most recent appearance in a major league game. Musgrove was a surprise addition to manager Craig Stammen's 26-man roster Tuesday before the Padres hosted the Chicago Cubs. Musgrove hasn't played for his hometown team since Oct. 2, 2024, when he left the Padres' clinching Wild Card Series victory over Atlanta with a right elbow injury. He underwent Tommy John surgery and missed the 2025 season, and he subsequently missed the entire 2026 regular season when his recovery progressed much more slowly than expected. Now 34 years old, Musgrove made four rehab appearances in August, but he said his postgame recoveries continued to be difficult. Musgrove has been throwing in instructional league games this month, and the Padres apparently liked what they saw. San Diego chose Musgrove for its 11-man postseason pitching staff over several possible candidates, including dependable right-hander Randy Vasquez, lefty reliever Wandy Peralta, trade deadline acquisition Casey Mize and Griffin Canning. Outfielder Miguel Andújar also was a surprising inclusion on the Padres’ roster. He hasn’t played since July 19 because of a broken wrist, but he took at-bats at Petco Park on Monday. Ethan Salas, the Padres' 20-year-old catcher, made the Wild Card Series roster as expected. If Salas plays in this series, he will become the youngest catcher ever to appear in the MLB postseason. Salas was called up Sept. 1, becoming the youngest player to catch a major league game since Iván "Pudge" Rodríguez in 1991. After a slow start, Salas finished the regular season with 10 hits in his last 24 at-bats. Reporting by the Associated Press.

articles.title: Stephen A Smith and ESPN should consider a full-time reunion with Skip Bayless
articles.summary: Skip Bayless returned to "First Take" for a monthly role, but a full-time reunion with Stephen A. Smith could revitalize ESPN's debate show.
articles.body: Last week, Skip Bayless returned to ESPN to reunite with his former debate partner, Stephen A. Smith, on "First Take." Under a new agreement, Bayless will appear on the program on the final Friday of every month. The history between Bayless and the show is significant. ESPN built "First Take," its daily debate program, around Bayless in 2007. Like Smith today, Bayless initially debated a rotating cast of analysts. He pushed the network to give Smith a recurring role, but executives initially resisted after Smith's previous, unsuccessful stint at ESPN. SKIP BAYLESS BOOSTS STEPHEN A'S SLUGGISH "FIRST TAKE" RATINGS BY 24% ON THEIR REUNION SHOW Smith eventually joined the show on a weekly basis and became Bayless' full-time debate partner in 2012. Together, Bayless and Smith drew an average audience that well exceeded ESPN2's typical viewership, often outperforming the main ESPN channel during the same time slot. Bayless left ESPN for FS1 in 2016 to launch "Undisputed," a similarly formatted debate program designed to compete directly with "First Take." Bayless partnered with Shannon Sharpe at FS1, while Max Kellerman replaced him at ESPN. Comparing the success of the two programs warrants context. ESPN reached three to five times as many morning viewers as FS1 at the time. Even so, "First Take" lost more than 20% of its audience after Bayless departed. ESPN responded by moving the program from ESPN2 to ESPN. After the move, "First Take" attracted roughly twice the audience of "Undisputed." The gap widened after Kellerman left "First Take" and Sharpe exited "Undisputed." By 2023, "First Take" regularly drew three to four times as many viewers as its FS1 rival. Bayless ultimately left the network in 2024. Smith and Bayless are in different positions than they were in 2012. At the time, Bayless was one of ESPN's most viral personalities. Smith had been relegated to local radio. Today, Smith is among the most influential figures in sports media, having recently signed a five-year, $100 million contract with ESPN. Until recently, Bayless was the one without a television platform. Bayless' transition to digital media has been rocky. His weekly show with his wife averages about 1,000 views per episode on YouTube. He has not uploaded a new episode of his eponymous podcast in nearly a year. He has, however, recently gained traction through a venture with former NFL cornerback Aqib Talib called "Gridiron." Although Bayless accepted an invitation to become a monthly contributor to "First Take," the arrangement is undoubtedly awkward. Returning to the program you built, alongside the co-host whose career you helped build, in a limited role cannot be easy. It is also reasonable to wonder whether Bayless believes Smith owes him the same full-time opportunity that he extended in 2012. OutKick asked Bayless about that possibility following Friday's show. He did not respond. Honestly, Smith should consider it. The current version of "First Take" has grown stale. The format of pairing Smith with two rotating panelists produces inconsistent results. Michael Irvin, Dan Orlovsky, Chris "Mad Dog" Russo and Marcus Spears are strong contributors. Much of the remaining rotation, however, consists of interchangeable ESPN personalities, including Chris Canty, Kimberley Martin and Domonique Foxworth. Perhaps a more effective approach would be to reduce the size of the rotation and feature only the program's strongest personalities alongside Smith and perhaps Bayless. On Friday, Spears joined Smith and Bayless for most of the show. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "First Take" is still one of ESPN's highest-rated programs, but its growth lags behind the network's other studio shows. ESPN's monthly press releases routinely emphasize year-over-year gains for "Get Up," "The Pat McAfee Show," "NFL Live" and other programs, but not "First Take's." Smith himself has acknowledged the importance of evolving the program. Explaining why he wanted Kellerman removed from the program, Smith said it was necessary "to keep things fresh and make changes every three years." It has now been five years since Kellerman's departure. Bayless also brings out a different side of Smith, one that is generally more appealing to viewers. The formula is simple but effective: Bayless makes a provocative claim, Smith responds with theatrical indignation, Bayless defends his position and the segment often ends in good fun. While not the most intellectually rigorous form of television, it's better than the pandering, faux sophistication that has come to define too much of sports television. Despite his branding, Smith rarely offers a profound opinion on sports. He believes the Cowboys underachieve, Stephen Curry is the greatest shooter in NBA history and LeBron James is the second-greatest player in basketball history. Those are conventional positions. In fact, Smith tends to expose a lack of depth when he tries to offer a unique opinion. His recent commentary on LSU, Shedeur Sanders and Deshaun Watson suggested a limited familiarity with those subjects. Smith performs best opposite a contrarian, like Bayless. The same dynamic explains why his appearances with Will Cain and Sean Hannity on Fox News often generate more interest than his solo political monologues. Smith, who has frequently responded to criticism from OutKick, may view that comparison as a slight. It is not. Michael Wilbon and Tony Kornheiser remain the gold standard of sports television because their partnership is stronger than either host individually. The same principle applies to Smith and Bayless. With Pat McAfee surpassing Smith as ESPN's most relevant personality, a full-time reunion with Bayless would represent an opportunity to regain momentum. Debating Chris Canty one day and Gerald McCoy the next does not. ESPN may be reluctant to approve a broader reunion for Bayless. Our understanding is that there was pushback about bringing him back even in a limited role. Executive Mike Foss, who oversees the network's daily studio programming, has emphasized a shift away from "embrace debate," the slogan that once defined "First Take," in favor of authenticity and conversation. Ratings trends suggest that approach has benefited much of ESPN's daytime lineup. But not "First Take." "First Take" is a debate show. The program has never fully recaptured the cultural relevance and virality it reached with Bayless and Smith together. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP If the plan is to keep Stephen A. in a prominent role as he approaches 60, ESPN should lean into what made him successful in sports-talk television. It is also 2026. As Hollywood continues to demonstrate, nostalgia remains a more reliable commercial strategy than reinvention.

articles.body:
After a long and eventful summer, hockey is officially back.

articles.title: Position grades from the Patriots’ loss to the Jaguars
articles.summary: Our film review of each position group after the Patriots’ 35-6 loss to the Jaguars.
articles.body:
No matter how you want to label it, the New England Patriots ' defeat against the Jacksonville Jaguars was a lopsided affair. While the team of head coach Mike Vrabel did have its chances to keep this a close game, it kept find a way to shoot itself in the foot on offense, defense and special teams. The final score of 35-6 is not a coincidence but a fair reflection of both teams' performances in Week 3.

Needless to say, and like we already discussed previously , most of the Patriots' was quite bad. And after watching the tape, we are ready to put some grades on their second loss of the year. Don't expect many good ones, though.

Quarterback: Questions about Drake Maye 's shoulder aside, the biggest issue that keeps plaguing him appears to be a mental one: once things start trending downwards, he finds himself in a spiral he can't get out of. The result is a quarterback looking for plays that aren't there to be made, and one actively making bad ones worse. Sure, his supporting cast is not necessarily playing its best football at the moment either — in part due to injuries — but Maye himself is not looking like the MVP runner-up he was last season either. Against the Jaguars, he had three more bad turnovers and despite Josh McDaniels relying on some of the Patriots' most basic concepts to get the pass game going finished with an EPA of -0.44. It was his seventh straight game with a negative expected points number, and another one where the good moments were dramatically outshone by the bad ones. As for Tommy DeVito , he did have a 20-yard completion to Romeo Doubs but overall looked like the backup he is. | Grade: D

Running back: Congratulations Corey Kiner on the longest carry by a Patriots running back on Sunday: your 7-yarder after Drake Maye was pulled takes the crown. That very much is all you need to know about New England 's run game versus the Jaguars. It was bad. A large part of it was the blocking (the three RBs gained only 10 combined yards before contact on the day) and a lack of schematic diversity (you can only run duo so much). The backs themselves also left some to be desired, however, with TreVeyon Henderson 's lack of vision and Rhamondre Stevenson 's uneven creativity both exacerbating the other problems. And it wasn't like Jacksonville sold out to stop the run, either; New England was unable to run into relatively light boxes all day. | Grade: C –

Wide receiver: There was some good and some bad from the wide receiver position. Mack Hollins continues to show a good rapport with Drake Maye, including on a well-timed 21-yard pickup on a curl route to convert a 3-and-5 on the opening drive; however, his fourth-quarter taunting penalty to turn 4th-and-1 into 4th-and-16 was as unnecessary as they get. DeMario Douglas had a 38-yard pickup in the second quarter and nearly connected with Maye on another big play later in the drive, but he still has not developed into the volume target you would want. His timing with Maye is simply off at times while his routes appear to be just a tad too imprecise for a steady down-to-down role. Speaking of which, Romeo Doubs has not provided that either and continues to be quiet as the supposed main man with A.J. Brown out. Kyle Williams and Efton Chism are non-factors, with the former's lack of production particularly frustrating: he very much remains a one-trick pony whose one trick doesn't look so powerful outside of preseason and who could have fought his way back to the ball on Maye's second INT. Chism, meanwhile, was in no position to catch Maye's first pick, but does deserve credit for salvaging the blown-up double pass in the second quarter by hitting Hollins for 16. | Grade: C

Tight end: It was a rough outing for a Patriots tight end group missing its secondary option, third-round rookie Eli Raridon. Hunter Henry was the clear No. 1 again, but he and Maye connected only once all game for a modest gain of 5 yards. His ability to beat zone coverage is still solid but the ball is simply not finding him as readily as it did a year ago. His blocking, meanwhile, is an issue — something that is also true for Cameron Latu , whose role on the team very much could come into question once players start returning from the injury lists. He did little as a run blocker (in fact, his presence very much might alert teams to what a play is going to be), had one penalty each on offense and special teams (and could have had a third had the officials not missed a face mask call in the first quarter), and was replaced by rookie Tanner Arkin down the stretch. | Grade: D

Offensive line: Let's start with the positives, namely the left side of the line. Will Campbell continues to look promising, while Alijah Vera-Tucker had possibly his best game yet next to him. The further right we go, the more problematic things get. Jared Wilson did bounce back as a pass blocker but failed to generate an adequate push in the run game; the right guard position lost their Mike Onwenu replacement, Greg Van Roten , in the first half and replaced him with first-timer Walter Rouse . It proved to be a downgrade from a downgrade both in the run game and in pass protection. Then, there was Morgan Moses , who looked as old as he ever has since joining the team last year. Maybe it was the foot injury he was dealing with heading into the game, but the veteran right tackle simply wasn't right before getting replaced by rookie Caleb Lomu — who was shaky himself — in the late third period. | Grade: C

Defensive line: The Patriots are missing Khyiris Tonga , and unless DaQuan Jones can fully replace him are in a vulnerable position along their interior defensive line versus the run — that is one of the big takeaways from Sunday's game. Cory Durden and Joshua Farmer simply do not have the size and raw power to consistently hold the line from the nose, and if Milton Williams and Christian Barmore have quiet days for whatever reason the interior is suddenly not as stout as it should be. One positive, however, was the play of young edges Elijah Ponder and Gabe Jacas : despite a heavy workload at an injury-ravaged position, they logged seven combined quarterback disruptions and were the most consistent source of pressure on the day. They were still a bit hit-or-miss with their assignments both against the run and the pass, but they are fairly low on the list of problems right now. | Grade: C+

Linebacker: Robert Spillane and Christian Elliss were among the best players on the field last week against the Steelers , but their impact was far less pronounced in Jacksonville. Elliss was solid again particularly coming downhill, but Spillane was a bit more inconsistent, His tackling (two misses) and spot-drops into coverage were especially uneven. Trevor Lawrence completed 11 of 14 downfield throws over the middle of the field — wisely staying away from the perimeter — and the linebacker's ability to defend his zones was part of the reason for his success. The second level wasn't bad per se, but it will continuously be challenged by opposing offenses if they see matchups they like. | Grade: C

Cornerback: Pay no attention to his PFF grade, Christian Gonzalez was again very good against the Jaguars. His only blemish was slipping on a third-down pass to Jakobi Meyers while coming out of his back-pedal, resulting in a 14-yard pickup. Other than that, he was excellent again in man or zone looks — prompting the Jaguars to simply look elsewhere for most of the day. This meant a busy day for Carlton Davis and Marcus Jones , who both gave up some completions as well. Jones giving up a 17-yard touchdown on third-and-goal while being outmuscled by Parker Washington was tough, and overshadowed what otherwise was a competitive outing that also included a second-quarter interception plus another near-pick later in the game. The biggest problem might not have been the cornerbacks' performance so much as how they were used: the Patriots fared well with a man-heavy game plan the first two weeks, but ditched it for more zone in Week 3. | Grade: B –

Safety: With two of the Patriots' top three safeties out, late-August trade pickup Jaylen Reed was moved into a starting role. His debut as the starter in place of an injured Craig Woodson was a mixed bag: he provided good coverage on the Marcus Jones interception, helping knock the ball into the air for his teammate to catch it. However, he missed a tackle on a 23-yard catch-and-run and was in coverage on Trevor Lawrence's touchdown pass to Jakobi Meyers to move the score to 14-3 in the late second quarter. Fellow starter Kevin Byard was relatively quiet outside of a hurry on a blitz, as was practice squad elevatee Mike Brown as the No. 3 at the position for this game. | Grade: C

Special teams: The Patriots have seen better days from their special teams group. While they did limit Parker Washington's impact as a punt returner, they gave up a 42-yard kickoff return and were unable to get their own return game going. Even when they did, a holding call against Cameron Latu backed the team up after a 31-yard runback. That was not the biggest problem for the group, though, which also saw Kyle Williams field a kickoff seemingly headed out of bounds for an effective net loss of 31 yards. To make matters worse, Andy Borregales shipped a 38-yard field goal try wide to the right at a point in the game where it was still competitive. | Grade: D

How would you grade the Patriots' performance against the Jaguars? Do you agree with our assessment? Please head down to the comment section to discuss with the rest of the community.

articles.title: Sidney Crosby knows he won’t play hockey forever. On the eve of his 22nd season, it’s hard to tell
articles.summary: While Crosby has stressed repeatedly that he wants to keep playing indefinitely, when the puck drops in Philadelphia on Wednesday night, it will mark the fir...
articles.body:
PITTSBURGH — It is the next-to-last day of September on the eve of Sidney Crosby 's 22nd season. His team's opener across the state in Philadelphia less than 36 hours away looms.

And there the longtime Pittsburgh Penguins captain is on a random early fall Tuesday, doing what he has always done: grinding through an hour-long practice with an intensity that shows no signs of waning as the player who arrived in the NHL as a teenage prodigy closes in on his 40th birthday.

Watch Crosby stand in front of the net and deftly deflect a point shot past rookie goaltender Sergei Murashov , who was still in diapers in his native Russia when Crosby made his NHL debut on Oct. 5, 2005. Watch Crosby fail to connect the dots on a pass on one end of the ice, then backcheck furiously before slapping his stick into the end boards in frustration.

Watch the NHL's seventh all-time leading scorer (soon to be in the top five) glide from the half wall to the front of the net and back again during a power play drill, the instincts that have carried him from franchise savior to Olympic gold medalist to three-time Stanley Cup champion taking over as he searches for an opportunity.

Practice breaks up. Some of Crosby's younger teammates head to the dressing room. Crosby does not. He remains on the ice for another 20-plus minutes with longtime teammates Evgeni Malkin and Kris Letang , chasing the finer points of a sport that has long doubled as an obsession.

Crosby's approach to his job is uncommon

Penguins coach Dan Muse heard about the trio's relentless drive when he took over in the summer of 2025. He wasn't skeptical, exactly, but seeing it up close gave him a different perspective.

"Sometimes I (was) surprised last year," Muse said. "Now I guess I'm not as surprised at how long they're out there for. ... I think for everybody who's seeing it too, like I said, it's not necessarily the normal."

And while Malkin and Letang have carved out their own unique places in NHL history during the trio's two decades together, it is Crosby who has always shouldered the load of outsized expectations that have followed him from Cole Harbour, Nova Scotia to Pittsburgh to, one day, the Hall of Fame.

It can be a lot. It already has been a lot. Yet Crosby has rarely let the burden show. Maybe because he's used to it. Or maybe because he doesn't really view it as a burden at all. Ask Crosby why he is still pushing himself at this pace, and he shrugs.

And not just when the lights come on and thousands of fans — many of them usually wearing some iteration of Crosby's jersey — come out to watch him do Sidney Crosby things. He is only player in NHL history to average a point a game for 21 straight seasons.

"I think, you know, there's the journey or the preparation that goes into it," he said.

It's why Crosby arrived at the team's practice facility weeks ahead of training camp. It's why he still seeks opportunities to compete internationally. Sure, he could have taken the summer off after Pittsburgh's surprising season ended with a loss to Philadelphia in the first round of the playoffs.

That's just not the way Crosby is wired. A few weeks after the postseason exit, he served as an alternate captain to 19-year-old San Jose Sharks sensation Macklin Celebrini for Team Canada at the 2026 World Championships. This after his hope for a second Olympic gold ended with an injury at the 2026 Cortina Winter Games.

It's a lot of hockey for anyone. Let alone someone who has been on "go" practically from the first time he pulled on skates.

Crosby wants to keep playing, but for how long he's not sure

And yet Crosby remains as passionate about all that goes into it now as he did when he was flinging pucks into an empty dryer in the basement of his childhood home.

"Ultimately, you just, every night you step on the ice, you're trying to win a hockey game," he said. "That's something that's still there. I think it provides a lot of fire to everything for me."

The flames show no signs of subsiding even while some of his contemporaries — Malkin and Alex Ovechkin of the Washington Capitals chief among them — seem to have the number of games ahead of them dwindling to a precious few.

The mix of nerves and excitement that accompanies every season opener is still there. Until they're not, expect Crosby to keep right on going.

While Crosby has stressed repeatedly that he wants to keep playing indefinitely, when the puck drops in Philadelphia on Wednesday night, it will mark the first time in his career that he will start a season in the final year of his contract. Crosby is in no hurry to sign anything; he learned a long time ago that he needs to listen to his body above all else.

"I don't think you ever know until you get to that point," Crosby told reporters when delivering season tickets to select fans earlier this month. "But I'm guessing it's your level, it's how your body feels, it's a combination of all those things. Overall, I feel pretty good."

Penguins general manager Kyle Dubas and Crosby's agent Pat Brisson have been in talks, but Dubas stressed on Monday that there isn't any "real pressure to have it done by a certain date or anything."

Stats are nice, but winning is all that matters

Crosby, who begins the year with 1,761 career points, 38 shy of passing Ron Francis for fifth on the all-time list, has no plans to coast to whatever the finish line looks like in hopes of piling up stats and paychecks.

When it's mentioned that 2,000 points — a plateau only Wayne Gretzky has reached — looks doable if he plays another handful of years, Crosby shakes his head. That's never been what this is about.

"I didn't even know how close I was until you just gave me that stat," he said. "So no, when you talk about motivating factors to play, I wouldn't say that's one of them."

The pathologically competitive Crosby remains intent on trying to help guide the Penguins back to the giddy heights of 2016 and 2017, when they became the first club in nearly 20 years to win back-to-back championships.

The going has grown increasingly tougher over the years. Pittsburgh hasn't advanced past the first round since 2018, though their promising run to second place in the Metropolitan Division last spring provided some tangible momentum. While Dubas plainly stated the goal this time around is to make inroads on division rival and reigning Cup champion Carolina, Crosby has no plans on looking that far ahead.

There is only the familiar rhythm of the season, with its practices and morning skates and overnight plane rides and team meals and — 84 times over the next six months, then hopefully a bit more after that — the chance to hop over the boards and lean into the fire once more.

articles.title: College Football analyst compares Oklahoma to Arkansas
articles.summary: College Football Analyst compares Oklahoma's performance against Georgia to Arkansas'.
articles.body:
The Oklahoma Sooners are coming off an embarrassing 41-13 road loss to the Georgia Bulldogs . The Sooners turned the ball over four times, three of them by quarterback John Mateer.

Mateer finished the game completing 25-of-34 passes for 231 yards, two touchdowns and those three turnovers. The Sooners also didn't get anything out of their rushing attack, rushing for just 65 yards on 35 carries.

This performance has resulted in a lot of public criticism. That includes SEC Network's Paul Finebaum, who compared the Sooners to an Arkansas Razorbacks team considered the worst in the SEC.

"Watching those games back-to-back, Georgia at Arkansas and Georgia at Oklahoma, Matt, tell me if you could tell the difference between Arkansas and Oklahoma," Finebaum said on 'The Matt Barrie Show.' "They both were inept."

Georgia also dismantled the Razorbacks earlier this season. They lost 45-17 in that game, and have just four wins in the last two seasons combined.

Finebaum's comparison reflects just how poor Oklahoma looked in Athens, but the Sooners still have time to change that perception. The bye week gives Brent Venables and his staff an opportunity to address the offensive issues, while the Red River Rivalry against the Texas Longhorns provides an immediate stage for Oklahoma to show that the Georgia performance was not representative of this team.

The Sooners don't need to erase the loss, but they do need to respond to it. A stronger performance against Texas would give Oklahoma a chance to turn the page and begin rebuilding the confidence that surrounded the program entering the season.

articles.title: When will Aaron Judge return from injury to the Yankees lineup in playoffs?

articles.body:
Of course the New York Yankees would love to have captain and three-time MVP in the lineup for the 2026 Wild Card series against the Boston Red Sox . But as he deals with what's being called "a moderate strain of the soleus muscle in his right calf" by MLB.com , he was left off the Wild Card roster.

So when will he return? After he received a PRP injection that could help the rehab process, he has taken some batting practice and has been throwing, but we'll see if he can run, which will be a big factor.

So the hope is that if the Yanks do advance, he could come back for the ALDS. But that's still very much up in the air at the moment.

articles.title: Panthers veteran pass catcher among top Week 4 waiver wire pickups
articles.summary: If you need a TE for your fantasy football team this week, Darren Waller could be worth a claim on the waiver wire.
articles.body:
The Carolina Panthers offense didn't have much going for it in Sunday's loss to the Cleveland Browns . One exception to the rule was the production they got in the passing game from their tight end room.

Mitchell Evans, Tommy Tremble and Darren Waller all did their part—as Waller came out on top with five grabs and 51 receiving yards. Through three weeks, Waller has been the team's best pass catcher at this spot, as expected—totaling 10 receptions, 112 yards and two touchdowns.

Going into Week 4, Waller has been named one of this week's best waiver wire pickups by Bleacher Report. Alex Kay writes:

Due to a rash of injuries to the Panthers' crop of pass-catchers, Waller wound up playing a much larger role than the one he assumed over the first two weeks of the campaign. He tallied his highest volume of offensive snaps (39), targets, receptions and receiving yardage since joining the club and could continue to build on those now that top receiver Jalen Coker has joined fellow wideout Xavier Legette on the injury report.

In addition to the injuries at wide receiver boosting his stock, Waller has a pretty juicy matchup this week. The Detroit Lions have allowed far more fantasy points to opposing tight ends this year than any other team, giving up 351 yards and six touchdowns.

NEW YORK – After a Monday night conversation with Aaron Judge , the Yankees decided to go without their slugging captain in the best-of-three Wild Card Series.

"Just felt like he's not quite there yet,' manager Aaron Boone said before Tuesday's Game 1 at Yankee Stadium against the rival Boston Red Sox .

"Hopefully…he spends these next few days continuing to work his way back and we'll see about being an option'' in a later 2026 postseason series, should the Yanks advance.

Yankees celebrate clinching AL playoff berth in photos

According to Boone, that "frank and honest'' talk, in which Judge accepted the Yanks' decision, included members of the team's athletic training staff.

Still, Boone said he'd been "encouraged by what I saw'' during Judge's live BP session Monday (but he did not run the bases).

"I don't think he's all the way back necessarily,'' said Boone. "But the fact he was able to (hit on the field required) a lot of boxes to check to get to that point. That's encouraging.''

Giancarlo Stanton hasn't taken a big-league at-bat since April 24, due to three separate calf strains, but "he's been in a pretty good place for a couple of weeks now,'' including a lot of hitting work.

"Credit to him for putting himself in a position to be an option,'' Boone said of carrying Stanton, who figures to be a pinch-hitter only in this series.

articles.title: Wigan's O'Neill wins Man of Steel award
articles.summary: Brad O'Neill wins the 2026 Steve Prescott MBE Man of Steel award as Wigan's Jenna Foubister wins Woman of Steel.
articles.body:
Wigan Warriors hooker Brad O'Neill has won the 2026 Steve Prescott MBE Man of Steel, the first time he has been given the honour.

The 24-year-old England hooker beat his Wigan team-mate Adam Keighran and Leeds full-back Lachie Miller to win the award.

O'Neill has been at the heart of an impressive Wigan side which won the Challenge Cup and League Leaders' Shield in 2026.

He made 31 appearances in all competitions and was also named Rugby League Writers and Broadcasters Association Player of the Year.

O'Neill was sin-binned in last year's Super League Grand Final for a wayward tackle on Tyrone May, however he inspired Wigan to two trophies, after a season without silverware in 2025.

It was a memorable night for the Warriors with Matt Peet also named Betfred Super League Coach of the Year having guided his side to the League Leaders' Shield and Challenge Cup.

Wigan earned a clean sweep in the final three shortlist for the Woman of Steel award as Eva Hunter, Jenna Foubister and Megan Willams were all nominated, with Foubister taking the prize.

It was the second year in a row that three Wigan players were shortlisted, however this year the Warriors missed out on adding the Women's Super League title to their Women's Challenge Cup and League Leaders' Crowns after they were beaten by York Valkyrie on Sunday.

Meanwhile, Halifax Panthers' Rob Hawkins won the Wheels of Steel award.

articles.title: Court injunction clears the way for Tamin Lipsey to rejoin Iowa State basketball
articles.summary: Lipsey has been added to Iowa State's roster after receiving a temporary restraining order in the Daley v. NCAA case.
articles.body:
AMES, Iowa — Tamin Lipsey has been added to Iowa State's roster after being granted an injunction for another year of eligibility last week.

Iowa State announced Lipsey's return on Monday with a social media post showing his No. 3 jersey hanging in his locker.

Lipsey went undrafted in the 2026 NBA draft, but played two NBA Summer League games with the Indiana Pacers before getting injured. He was granted a temporary restraining order by an Indiana judge last week for one of the numerous lawsuits filed against the NCAA for its new eligibility rules.

Lipsey averaged 13.5 points, 5.1 assists, 3.9 rebounds and 2.3 steals per game last season on a team that reached the NCAA Tournament's Sweet 16. The 6-foot-1 guard was an Associated Press honorable mention All-American in 2024 and is a three-time all-Big 12 selection.

Lipsey is the first player in Big 12 history to eclipse 1,500 points, 600 assists, 500 rebounds and 300 steals in a career.

articles.title: Steelers news: Mike McCarthy still won't commit to Joey Porter Jr. Week 4 return
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers haven’t had the services of star defensive back Joey Porter Jr. this season. Porter has been injured. Even though he has been listed...
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers haven't had the services of star defensive back Joey Porter Jr. this season. Porter has been injured. Even though he has been listed as a full participant in a recent Steelers practice, Pittsburgh head coach Mike McCarthy is not sure that Porter will play.

"We hope so," McCarthy said when asked if Porter would play in Pittsburgh's Week 4 contest, per The Athletic.

Porter also has been looking for a new contract with the team. A deal didn't materialize before the start of the season. The Steelers don't typically engage in contract talks during the season. That is why Porter apparently won't get a new deal anytime soon.

Reports have swirled that the Steelers may trade Porter, and the Detroit Lions and Dallas Cowboys have been listed as possible trade partners. Time will tell if the defensive back is on the move soon.

During the 2025 season, Porter posted 52 total tackles for Pittsburgh. That included 35 solo stops. He has been a key cog in the Steelers secondary over the last few seasons.

McCarthy added more information when asked about Porter's status.

"We've got a plan for Joey," said McCarthy, per the team. "Hopefully he'll do more, give him a chance to get out there. He's in the same situation that anybody is coming off of a medical situation. Hopefully we can make progress.

"We all would love to see Joey play, and I'd love the opportunity to coach him."

Pittsburgh is 2-1 on the season. The Steelers had their best game offensively of the season in a Week 3 win over the Cincinnati Bengals .

The Steelers play the Cleveland Browns in Week 4 of the NFL season. That contest is scheduled for Thursday.

articles.title: Yamal inspires Spain to Croatia romp on World Cup homecoming
articles.summary: Lamine Yamal scored two goals and set up another as Spain hammered Croatia 4-1 on Tuesday in the Nations League in their first home game since lifting the Wo...
articles.body:
Lamine Yamal scored two goals and set up another as Spain hammered Croatia 4-1 on Tuesday in the Nations League in their first home game since lifting the World Cup.

Yamal, 19, was joined on the scoresheet by Marc Pubill and Nico Williams as they extended their unbeaten run to 40 matches, which includes June's final triumph over Argentina in the United States.

La Roja next play Czech Republic on Saturday in Group A3.

Yamal's contribution strengthened his case for the Ballon d'Or, with voting having closed on Monday and the winner announced on October 26.

"We've enjoyed his magic in the service of the team. In the future, he'll be much more recognised for what he does and for his contribution to the team's play," Spain coach Luis de la Fuente told Teledeporte.

Captain Rodri showed off the World Cup trophy before kick-off at the packed Estadio Ramon Sanchez-Pizjuan, being handed it by Sevilla legend Jesus Navas , a winner with Spain in 2010.

"We were very excited to bring the trophy here," Yamal said.

"To be able to win the game and bring it home is great," he added.

Attackers Yamal, Alex Baena and Mikel Oyarzabal started the game having scored in Saturday's thrilling 3-2 win over England at Wembley.

Croatia made six changes from the weekend's win over the Czech Republic, leaving icon Luka Modric on the bench.

Yamal opened the scoring within two minutes against the Three Lions and took just 75 seconds to do so against Slaven Bilic's side in Andalusia.

Just before the half-hour mark, the visitors equalised through Dion Beljo's header as the 1.95m-tall attacker headed home from an Ivan Perisic cross.

Two minutes later the hosts restored their lead as Pubill fired home a header from a pin-point Yamal cross.

Just 45 seconds before the interval, the home side were denied a third goal by the post as Fermin Lopez failed to find the bottom corner.

Yamal claimed his second after 63 minutes, beating Barcelona team-mate and Croatia goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic at his near post.

The teenager's second took his tally of international goals to 10 in 35 appearances.

With fewer than two minutes to play, Athletic Bilbao 's Williams notched up a fourth for Spain with a crisp dribble and finish.

"The first half could have ended 4–1 or 5–1, and the second half was more of the same," De la Fuente said.

"We were up against a team that defends well and is strong in the air, so you have to be on your toes in every situation. But then we regained possession, our passing and control of the game."

articles.title: Browns Week 4: Scouting the Pittsburgh Steelers- Something new or the same as always?
articles.summary: Week 4 for the Cleveland Browns sees the same Pittsburgh Steelers team, with some key changes
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns prepare for their AFC North opener against their hated rival, the Pittsburgh Steelers . Like the Browns, the Steelers underwent a coaching change this past offseason, but when it comes to their quarterback situation, this will be the last season we see quarterback Aaron Rodgers play in the NFL. On paper, Pittsburgh returns the same team that made the postseason last year but made minor tweaks.

Mike Tomlin is now working for NBC Sports. After spending a year away from coaching, Mike McCarthy is now coaching the Pittsburgh Steelers . If Mike McCarthy has an NBA head coach counterpart, he would be Doc Rivers (who also works for NBC Sports). Outside of one championship that he won, McCarthy's resume is average at best. His departure from the Packers was somewhat messy, but he was later hired by the Dallas Cowboys .

Despite having numerous winning seasons with the Cowboys, McCarthy could never get them out of the divisional round, despite some years of the team having the talent to make a deep playoff run.

It's too early to tell if going from Tomlin to McCarthy is an upgrade, but McCarthy's coaching staff is slightly better than Tomlin's staff from last year.

In regard to the quarterback, Aaron Rodgers will retire after this season. Rodgers hasn't been as good during his prime, but he is still showing that he's capable of being a competent quarterback despite his clear limitations.

It's too early to tell, but no one knows how good the Steelers are. On paper, the roster seems the exact same as last year despite a couple of new additions. Despite the team being 2-1, the two wins that the Steelers have aren't exactly impressive . The Atlanta Falcons could've beaten them if quarterback Cooper Rush didn't start, and special teams is the reason why the Cincinnati Bengals couldn't leave Pittsburgh with a win. The ceiling/floor still remains the same, but it's hard to imagine this team actually making a deep playoff run due to their limitations eventually catching up to them. This team isn't bad, but it's hard to say if they are actually good.

The one unit that has slowly dropped off over the years is Steelers defense. Maybe not anymore. Defensive coordinator Teryl Austin was a liability, and going from Austin to Patrick Graham was an upgrade. The unit remains the same on paper, but on the field, the defense looks different.

Linebacker T.J. Watt is being moved around and not relegated to one spot, defensive tackle Cam Heyward is still defying Father Time, and defensive tackle Derrick Harmon seems to be making the leap. The secondary has some reliable veterans in Jalen Ramsey and Jamel Dean , but the situation surrounding Joey Porter Jr . is one that can't be ignored. Porter Jr. hasn't played this season, but he could play on Thursday night. After not reaching a new deal on a contract, Porter Jr could be traded to another team and the Steelers would be open to it.

Overall, this unit could be better than what we have seen in recent years.

The San Diego Padres host the Chicago Cubs in Game 1 of the National League wild card series on Tuesday at Petco Park, with each team looking to take a huge step towards the next round.

It's a rematch of last year's wild card series, won by the Cubs at Wrigley Field in Chicago. Right-hander Michael King will start the opener for the Padres, with southpaw Matthew Boyd taking the mound for the Cubs.

"Very professional lineup," King said of the Cubs' offense. "They were first in runs this year and it shows."

The Padres are trying to get back to the World Series for the first time since 1998 and are in the postseason for the fourth time in five years, undoubtedly the most successful spell in the franchise's history.

"It's a new year, it's a different year," Padres third baseman Manny Machado said. "Obviously, that stung last year for us. They played better ball than us last year. This year's going to be a little bit different. "
