articles.title: Where do Legend Bey, Khary Wilder and other Ohio State football freshmen stand?
articles.summary: Several Ohio State freshmen flashed in limited roles in September. Could bigger opportunities be ahead for Legend Bey, Khary Wilder and others?
articles.body:
Ohio State has seen a handful of freshmen flash as playmakers in September.

Jay Timmons emerged as the starting nickel back following a strong offseason. His hit on the first play from scrimmage at Texas led to a fumble he recovered. He has broken up four passes.

Other newly arrived players have stood out in more limited roles as backups.

It was in the Buckeyes' season-opening win over Ball State when running back Legend Bey turned a swing pass into a dazzling touchdown, crisscrossing the turf at Ohio Stadium to reach the end zone.

Defensive end Khary Wilder has generated pressure rotating as part of third-down packages, while wide receivers Brock Boyd and Chris Henry Jr. have made several deep catches.

Here's where these other freshmen stand entering October:

Bey made an appearance early in the loss at Texas on Sept. 12, catching a backward pass on Ohio State's second drive. It was a chance to get him the ball in space, where his speed and wiggle make him difficult to bring down.

But linebacker Rasheem Biles , a Pickerington Central grad, snuffed out the pass and tackled Bey for a loss of a yard.

It was the only snap Bey played against the Longhorns. Despite his early involvement in the high-profile matchup, he never rotated back in at running back again or returned kickoff as he had in the previous week.

A tweaked ankle then limited him to just four snaps against Kent State on Sept. 19, and he did not play against Illinois on Sept. 26, though he was not listed on the Buckeyes' unavailable list submitted to the Big Ten for their conference opener. He has lined up as a kickoff returner just once since he did not signal for fair catches against Ball State.

"We all know his ability level," Buckeyes coach Ryan Day said. "Just got to continue to work to build trust. We'd like to see him on the field."

Day said Bey's immediate role at Iowa on Oct. 3 would depend on what he shows in practices this week.

There is incentive for the Buckeyes to find a role for him given their need for explosiveness out of the backfield. Ohio State had just three runs of 20 yards or more through Week 4, fewer than all but 25 out of the 138 teams in the Football Bowl Subdivision.

Nine Ohio State defensive linemen have played more snaps than Wilder through four games, according to Pro Football Focus.

But the smaller role has not limited Wilder's production, as he has shown potential as a pass rusher, leading the Buckeyes with four hurries.

Wilder's twitchiness combined with his 6-foot-4, 257-pound frame makes him an intriguing piece as the Buckeyes search for more havoc up front.

"We need production for sure," Day said. "We're taking all applications."

Wilder has lined up as a defensive end and as an interior lineman in pass-rushing situations.

"That's our wild card," defensive end Kenyatta Jackson Jr. said. "We put him on the field, and it's, 'See ball, go get ball.' That's what we tell him."

The streamlining of his role has allowed him to provide immediate production.

"He does a fantastic job of doing it," Jackson said.

Most of Wilder's appearances have been on passing downs. Of his 49 snaps, he has rushed the passer on 35 of them, per PFF.

When Day was asked about Wilder's role, he stressed the need for players to be disciplined in their assignments.

"It's one thing to have talent, it's one thing to flash," Day said, "but when you're playing team defense and one guy is not where you're supposed to be, I'm not talking about any player in particular, but it does matter, and I think we all need to recognize that.

"All it takes is one guy to be out of a gap and it can turn into an explosive play. We all have to be disciplined in what we do. We don't just go out there and make plays. We have to play within the defensive scheme."

While Boyd and Henry have been in the receiver rotation since the opening week, they had larger roles against Illinois.

Henry played 25 snaps and Boyd saw 22 snaps, the third- and fourth-most among the Buckeyes' receivers, per PFF.

They also carried more of the trust of quarterback Julian Sayin.

When the Buckeyes began a drive at their 4-yard line in the second quarter, Sayin found Henry on a pass over the middle for 15 yards.

Sayin later connected with Boyd for a 22-yard completion on a game-sealing drive in the fourth quarter. Boyd caught the pass along the sideline before keeping himself in bounds and tip toeing for a few more yards.

"They have a couple games under their belt," Sayin said, "and they're just getting better each week."

Joey Kaufman covers Ohio State football for The Columbus Dispatch. Email him at jkaufman@dispatch.com and follow him on @joeyrkaufman on X.

articles.title: Rams news: Sean McVay hopeful for key secondary reinforcement to return in Week 4
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay is hopeful the team’s secondary will receive a key reinforcement with safety Kamren Kinchens potentially returning for...
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay is hopeful the team's secondary will receive a key reinforcement with safety Kamren Kinchens potentially returning for a Week 4 road matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles .

The Rams enter the week at 1-2 after suffering a 30-26 loss to the Denver Broncos on Sunday Night Football. As Los Angeles attempts to bounce back, Kinchens could make his return after dealing with a hamstring injury.

Rams team writer Stu Jackson shared an update on Kinchens' status Tuesday via X, formerly known as Twitter.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"On The Coach McVay Show with @JB_Long, Rams HC Sean McVay said they are 'hopeful' they'll get safety Kamren Kinchens (hamstring) back this week."

Kinchens' potential return would provide Los Angeles with another option in the secondary as it prepares to face an Eagles team that enters Week 4 with a 2-1 record.

Kamren Kinchens could provide boost for Sean McVay, Rams

Los Angeles will look to rebound after letting a significant advantage slip away against Denver.

The Rams built a 16-0 halftime lead over the Broncos before Denver rallied in the second half. Los Angeles still had an opportunity to retake the lead late, but quarterback Matthew Stafford threw an interception on the potential game-winning drive.

The loss dropped the Rams below .500 through the opening three weeks of the season after they earned their first victory with a 28-6 win over the New York Giants in Week 2 .

Getting Kinchens back would give McVay and the Rams some additional help as they attempt to avoid a second consecutive loss. His status throughout the practice week should provide more clarity on whether he will be ready to return against Philadelphia.

The Rams will travel to face the Eagles on Sunday at 10 a.m. PT.

articles.title: Breaking down the college sports act: A salary cap, a 'Lane Kiffin rule' and a superleague ban
articles.summary: The Senate passed a bill Monday night that would bring new rules to college sports covering a wide range of issues including how schools pay their players, w...
articles.body:
The Senate passed a bill Monday night that would bring new rules to college sports covering a wide range of issues including how schools pay their players, what those players can and cannot go to court to fight, and how many transfers players can make. The 77-22 votes sends the The Protect College Sports Act to the House, where supporters are hoping the large margin and bipartisan nature of the bill will give it momentum to pass before the end of the year. Among the key provisions:

The bill would put into law the revenue sharing that was negotiated under terms of the House settlement , which allows schools to share up to 22% of certain revenue with athletes. This year, that amounts to $21.58 million per school. It also would add a $27.5 million "retention pool" that can be used to keep current players on the roster and is designed to bring many of the third-party name, image and likeness payments from "associated entities" affiliated with the schools under the new cap.

The bill offers the NCAA some protection against lawsuits in several areas, most notably on eligibility issues that have landed the governing body in court dozens of times over the past year. Most recently, the lawsuits are coming from players who graduated high school in 2022 and were denied a fifth year of college eligibility under a new rule that kicks in for the Class of '23.

The bill limits sports agents to receiving a maximum of 5% of an athlete's endorsement contract.

The legislation is intended to preempt state laws, many of which were passed over the past five years to regulate NIL within state borders, that conflict with the guidelines set by the national law. Exactly how this plays out could be subject to litigation.

The bill would generally limit athletes to one "free" transfer without having to sit out a season, a move that could cut down on some of the chaos and expenses created by the constant need to recruit and pay players out of the transfer portal. Athletes went to court in recent years to win the right to transfer without penalty.

The bill would prohibit coaches from leaving one school for another during the season. An amendment proposed by Sen. Cory Booker, D-N.J., that would have restricted coaching salaries to $5 million per year lost on a largely party line vote.

In a rewrite of a 1961 law that prohibited this, the legislation would give college athletic conferences the option of pooling their media rights in an effort to generate more revenue. The powerful Southeastern and Big Ten conferences don't agree it would make more money and have resisted this effort.

The bill would require most schools to maintain the same number of Olympic-sport programs as they had in the 2024-25 school year for at least nine years. Also, $5 million of each school's new retention pool would be devoted to women's and Olympic sports.

The measure would provide federal funding for broadband and media infrastructure at historically Black college and university programs.

The bill would also prohibit conferences from expanding beyond 20 teams and adds other measures to prevent the creation of a breakaway "superleague." The number went up from 19 to 20 after a voice vote for an amendment offered by Sen. Ashley Moody, R-Fla.

articles.title: It is time for Tuchel to offer Alexander-Arnold some trust
articles.summary: Having been overlooked for so long, Trent Alexander-Arnold produced a world-class moment on his return, writes Phil McNulty.
articles.body:
England head coach Thomas Tuchel's apparent lack of trust in Trent Alexander-Arnold has been one of the defining features - and a constant narrative - of his time in charge.

The 27-year-old right-back has won a Premier League title at Liverpool then moved to Real Madrid since he last started for England, selected as a left-back by interim manager Lee Carsley when scoring in a 3-1 Nations League win in Finland in October 2024.

He was ignored for England's World Cup squad last summer, despite right-back being a cursed role for Tuchel, making it appear that whatever questions the German had about that position, Alexander-Arnold was never going to be the answer.

So Tuchel's decision to recall Alexander-Arnold for this four-game Nations League camp came as a surprise, so emphatically had he been marginalised by England.

It was against this backdrop that Alexander-Arnold became the ninth right-back used by Tuchel in 24 games when he finally got his start against Czech Republic in Prague as England tried to recover from the 3-2 loss to World Cup holders Spain at Wembley.

And, with perhaps something to prove according to Tuchel, Alexander-Arnold did exactly that in one world-class moment that might convince his coach to train his sights on what he can do rather than what he cannot.

It is time, in other words, for Tuchel to offer Alexander-Arnold some trust.

England, despite being in control, were toiling against the 10-man Czechs, who had seen danger man Pavel Sulc sent off after only 25 minutes for a reckless challenge on Elliot Anderson .

It was then, two minutes after the break, that Alexander-Arnold delivered a moment beyond those Tuchel has chosen ahead of him at right-back to pierce that stubborn resistance.

The player now officially known as "Trent", according to the name on the back of his shirt, had already made a 70-yard run into an attacking position in an attempt to increase England's attacking options.

When the move broke down, he regained possession before unfurling a magnificent right-foot delivery that floated in a teasing arc beyond three Czech defenders for Anthony Gordon to score with a stooping header that he made look far easier than it actually was.

Of course, Tuchel may still harbour those reservations about Alexander-Arnold's defending, and they were not put to the test here, but these few seconds showed exactly what he is about and what he can rightly argue is his unique selling point.

The defensive questions must wait for another day. The answers, whenever they come, would appear to shape Tuchel's thinking and Alexander-Arnold's England career, but he deserves the opportunity to provide them.

A delighted Tuchel told BBC Radio 5 Live: "He (Alexander-Arnold) did very well. He had an excellent assist. Overall, like everyone, he was professional, top attitude and one decisive action."

He added: "We never doubted that he can produce these kinds of assists. The deeper position in the second half suited him more than the higher position in the first half.

"Overall, I think we had a good and professional performance. Of course, the red card, especially an early red card, is such a heavy influence in the game. It makes the task sometimes a little bit more complicated psychologically."

'This must be close to make or break time'

Gordon, the grateful beneficiary of Alexander-Arnold's class, said: "I make that run time and time again and only a certain number of players have that ability, technique and bravery to be willing to make the mistake trying that pass. That's why he's so good and I've been dying to play with him for that reason.

"He's had his own journey with England. He would've liked to have played more than he has but he's been a great character during this camp. I've really enjoyed being around him."

Alexander-Arnold is a risk taker, both in the defensive and attacking context, but only Elliot Anderson (41) made more passes in the final third than he did (32), while only Anthony Gordon, with four, created more chances than the defender's three.

Tuchel, it should be stated, is not alone in having doubts about Alexander-Arnold.

Who can forget – although many would love to – Sir Gareth Southgate's ill-fated attempt to utilise Alexander-Arnold as a midfielder at Euro 2024? It was ditched after 54 minutes of England's second game against Denmark never to be seen again.

More will be revealed if Tuchel persists with Alexander-Arnold against Croatia behind closed doors in Rijeka on Saturday – but this must be close to make or break time for this lavishly-talented player who is 28 on 7 October.

If he cannot convince Tuchel in this camp, and surely that one moment of game-changing skill must be fixed in the head coach's mind, then you wonder if he ever will.

Alexander-Arnold said: "It was amazing. It's always an honour to represent my country. It's been a long time, but I've always believed I can play for England. That belief has always been there and it was about proving it at club level. The manager gave me a chance, now hopefully he is happy with how I played."

Alexander-Arnold, however, could not have done any more as England, who sealed the three points with captain Harry Kane 's 87th goal in 123 international appearances, got their Nations League campaign going in Prague.

articles.title: J.J. McCarthy Gets New Jersey Number With New York Giants
articles.summary: Former Michigan QB J.J. McCarthy will wear No. 18 with the New York Giants after No. 9 was unavailable following his trade from Minnesota.
articles.body:
J.J. McCarthy is officially starting over in New York , and apparently that includes his jersey number.

After being acquired by the New York Giants from the Minnesota Vikings for a 2027 fifth-round pick, the former Michigan quarterback will wear No. 18 with his new team.

McCarthy wore No. 9 during his championship-winning career at Michigan and kept the number after Minnesota selected him No. 10 overall in the 2024 NFL Draft. But No. 9 wasn't available in New York because tight end Isaiah Likely already owns it. The Giants assigned No. 9 to Likely after signing him during the offseason , and the team's current roster still lists him with that number.

The number change is a small detail, but an interesting one considering how closely McCarthy has been associated with No. 9 throughout his career.

The much bigger story, of course, is the fresh start. New York acquired the 23-year-old McCarthy after losing Jaxson Dart for the remainder of the regular season , though Jameis Winston remains the Giants' starting quarterback for now.

McCarthy went 27-1 as Michigan's starting quarterback and helped lead the Wolverines to the 2023 national championship before his NFL career got off to a rocky start in Minnesota.

Now he'll try to revive that career in New York.

And, for the first time in quite a while, a new number.

articles.title: DWCS fight canceled hours prior to event after UFC hopeful falls ill
articles.summary: These UFC hopefuls will still square off – just not tonight.
articles.body:
An illness has forced a bout off Tuesday's Dana White's Contender Series 94 event.

Ilias Bulaid has fallen ill. As a result, his bout vs. Erick Visconde has been rescheduled to the season finale on Oct. 13, the promotion announced just hours before Tuesday's episode.

A lengthy explanation was posted on Bulaid's Instagram account shortly after news of the postponement surfaced. Written in the third person, the statement explains that Bulaid (9-0) came down with an infection over the past few days, made worsened by his weight cut.

"It is with great disappointment that we have to announce that Ilias will not be able to compete tonight. A few days before the weigh-in, he began experiencing stomach and abdominal issues, as did some of his coaches and trainers. From that moment on, we remained in close contact with the UFC Medical Team and had the situation carefully assessed. The weight cut went entirely according to plan. Ilias only had to lose 2.5 kg and made weight in a controlled manner. The UFC Medical Team confirmed that his condition was not a result of the weight cut.

"Unfortunately, the infection continued to worsen, partly due to his weakened immune system. As a result, we have spent more time in the hospital than at the hotel over the past few days. Following a medical assessment, the UFC doctor determined that it would not be safe for Ilias to fight.

"This is, of course, a huge disappointment for Ilias and the entire team. We did everything within our power, but ultimately, this situation was beyond our control. Our focus is now on his recovery. Thank you to everyone for your support and understanding."

articles.title: White Sox receive a letter from Pope Leo XIV on day of playoff opener
articles.summary: The Chicago White Sox received a letter from Pope Leo XIV on the same day of their playoff opener against the Houston Astros.  The Sept. 9 letter was address...
articles.body:
HOUSTON (AP) — The Chicago White Sox received a letter from Pope Leo XIV on the same day of their playoff opener against the Houston Astros .

The Sept. 9 letter was addressed to White Sox owner Jerry Reinsdorf, and the team said it arrived at Chicago's Rate Field on Tuesday ahead of Game 1 of its AL Wild Card Series against the Astros.

Leo is a White Sox fan dating to his days growing up in Chicago. He was known as Robert Prevost or Father Bob when he went to the World Series opener 21 years ago, a 5-3 White Sox victory over the Astros.

The pontiff began his note by thanking Reinsdorf for the letter he sent after the team paid tribute to Leo during an Aug. 11 game against Cincinnati .

"It is my hope that the White Sox will continue to foster bonds of friendship and solidarity among people, and thus bear hopeful witness to the possibility of living and working together in peace," Leo wrote.

"With these sentiments, I willingly invoke the Almighty's abundant blessings upon you and your loved ones."

The White Sox earned an AL wild card this year by finishing with an 84-78 record. They lost at least 101 games in each of the previous three seasons.

Asked recently if he had a hand in the team's surprising turnaround, the smiling pontiff responded "No comment."

articles.title: Who 'battled impressively' for Scots? And how did you rate players?
articles.summary: How Scotland's players rated in their Nations League defeat by Switzerland.
articles.body:
Scotland were well beaten by Switzerland in their second Nations League match, as the visitors cruised to victory in Sebastian Pocognoli's first home game in charge.

Jack Hendry 's 11th-minute red card proved too much for the Scots to overcome as they fell to a 3-0 defeat.

Here's how we rated Scotland's players - and you can give your marks below.

Angus Gunn – Beaten on his side of the goal by Ricardo Rodriguez 's powerful free-kick for the opening goal. Good saves either side of half-time to deny Ndoye , but beaten by power again for Zeki Amdouni 's third goal. 4

Jack Hendry – Roasted for pace by Dan Ndoye and clumsily brought the striker down to earn a deserved red card, leaving Scotland down to 10 early on. 2

Luis Binks – Brondby defender's first act was a rash late tackle. Slow to close down Ndoye and prevent the cross that set up Nico Elvedi for Switzerland's second goal, but otherwise did not look out of place. 6

Scott McKenna – The majority of the Swiss threats came from wide but defender dealt with most of what came his way. 6

Nathan Patterson – Had his hands full with the pacy Ndoye down Switzerland's left. Struggled to make any impression as an attacking force. 5

Andy Robertson – Usual willingness to get up and down the left flank yielded little reward on his 99th Scotland appearance. 6

Lewis Ferguson – A few timely interventions on the edge of his own box, but saw little of the ball as the Swiss midfield took firm control. 5

Billy Gilmour – Looked most likely to make something happen for Scotland in early stages but faded as the Swiss took control and hooked before the hour mark. 5

John McGinn – Struggled to influence the game in the way we know he can. Scotland need to find a way to get him into the positions where he can do some damage. 5

Kieron Bowie – Sacrificed early for Stephen Welsh following Hendry's red card. 5

Oli McBurnie – Battled impressively as a lone striker after Bowie's departure and caused problems for the Swiss defence. 7

Stephen Welsh (Bowie 13') – Brought on to shore up defence after Hendry's red card. Played his part in steadying the ship before Switzerland doubled their lead. 6

Ryan Christie (Gilmour 59') – Got half an hour but made little impression. 5

Ben Gannon-Doak (Patterson 59') – Spent most of his time chasing back towards his own goal. 5

Robbie Ure (McBurnie 59') – Got no service to work with. 5

Josh Doig (Robertson 74') – Subbed on when the Swiss had all but killed off the game. 5

Subs not used: Scott Bain , Liam Kelly , Aaron Hickey , Luke Graham, Lennon Miller , Josh McPake , Kristi Montgomery.

articles.title: Hampden debut to forget but Pocognoli looks at bigger picture
articles.summary: Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli hopes "we will remember this night differently later on" as his Hampden bow ends with a 3-0 defeat by Switzerland.
articles.body:
Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli hopes to "remember this night differently later on" after his Hampden debut ended in a deflating Nations League defeat by Switzerland .

Off the back of a goalless draw in Ljubljana on Saturday in his first game as Scotland boss, Pocognoli's side slumped to a 3-0 loss in Glasgow's southside on Tuesday.

Scotland are now without a clean sheet in eight home matches and, perhaps more worryingly, have failed to score in six of their nine games this year.

Pocognoli promised a more attacking approach, built on a high press and high energy, but those ideals were undermined by Jack Hendry 's 11th-minute red card.

Ricardo Rodriguez rifled the subsequent free-kick past Angus Gunn and the Swiss never ceded control, with Leeds United centre-back Nico Elvedi and Burnley midfielder Zeki Amdouni adding to the scoreline in the second half.

The Scots are third in their Nations League group after two games, with a trip to bottom side North Macedonia on Saturday before the visit of Slovenia on Tuesday.

"It's not easy against a good team to be with 10 men," said Pocognoli, who was appointed as Steve Clarke's successor in August.

"It will be more about the reaction. We had an unlucky red card, punished with the free-kick, that's the worst scenario. The guys did the best they could and hopefully we will remember this night differently later on.

"We have to move on and get a good result in North Macedonia."

articles.title: Jared Verse’s pressure surge is lifting the Browns pass rush, even without the sacks
articles.summary: Jared Verse is making his impact felt on the Cleveland Browns defense, even though he hasn't had a sack.  The third-year edge rusher leads the Browns with ni...
articles.body:
BEREA, Ohio (AP) — Jared Verse is making his impact felt on the Cleveland Browns defense, even though he hasn't had a sack.

The third-year edge rusher leads the Browns with nine quarterback pressures this season. He had six in last Sunday's 21-18 victory over Carolina , including three where he collapsed the pocket around quarterback Bryce Young , allowing Mason Graham and Isaiah McGuire to get the sacks.

Verse also had a quarterback hit and five hurries against the Panthers .

"I think the measure of a great player is how you can elevate those around you," Verse said on Tuesday as the Browns prepared for Thursday night's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers . "Even if I'm not getting the stats that I want, every player wants, as long as my teammate and as long as we get the W, that's all that matters. That's what I get paid for."

Getting consistent pressure without it leading to sacks has been a way of life for Verse, who was acquired from the Los Angeles Rams in the Myles Garrett trade. He has generated 152 pressures since entering the league in 2024, fifth most among edge rushers. However, he has only a 7.9% sack conversion rate, second lowest among players with at least 600 pass rush snaps.

Among the top 10 edge rushers the past two-plus seasons, no other player has a pressure-to-sack rate below 11.5%.

Another reason why Verse had success against the Panthers is because defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg moved him around more. After lining up only as an edge rusher the first two weeks, Verse saw some snaps in the box at defensive end and defensive tackle.

"When you put speed up in the middle, it throws off the guys on the interior. When you got power rushers on the edge, it throws everybody off," he said. "I mean, the interior guys don't really do a lot of scout reports on me because I don't rush over them a lot. So when I am over them, it gets them in a stressful situation and I think that's what we took advantage of."

Verse worked on a bunch of new pass rush moves and techniques during training camp and the preseason. With the new moves not working, he decided to go back to basics.

"I think I listened too much to other people. Everybody's talking about, 'Oh, you need this move, you need that move.' And I forgot where it got me to the point I'm at, which was genuinely just running through your face," he said. "If you're not stronger than me, I don't care how these guys are 320, 330 (pounds), it doesn't matter. I'll still run through. You're going backwards while I'm going forwards at full speed, I'm just going to run through you. So I forgot that's my superpower."

Coach Todd Monken lauded Verse for going back to what works best for him.

"He wants to get to the quarterback, he wants to disrupt the game, and I think he's right in terms of just, like, 'all right, what can I do, right, what is it that I do well, and don't try to be anybody else but yourself, and be the best version you can of yourself.' And I think he's bought into that and really affected the quarterback," Monken said.

The Browns go into Thursday night's game with a 42.5% pressure rate, second highest in the league. They are also one of three teams with five players who have had at least seven pressures this season.

Cleveland has had at least nine players have multiple pressures in each of the past two weeks, only the third team to do that in consecutive weeks since 2018.

The Browns pass rush will be in for a tough test against Pittsburgh's Aaron Rodgers , who has one of the quickest releases in the league. Rodgers completed 6 of 11 passes for 121 yards and a touchdown against Cincinnati last week while under pressure.

"That's who he is as a player. When you get those kind of releases, you can't let it frustrate you as a D-line. You just got to keep rushing.," Verse said. "At one point he's going to hold that for two, three seconds, and that's when you got to take advantage of him."

articles.title: This Red Sox Hype Video Will Pump Boston Fans Up Ahead of 2026 MLB Playoffs
articles.summary: NESN chronicled the Red Sox's incredible turnaround ahead of the team's playoff series against the Yankees.
articles.body:
The Red Sox weren't supposed to be here.

At least, that's the story the first half of the 2026 season seemed to be telling.

Boston endured one of the worst starts in franchise history, struggled offensively, dealt with a string of injuries and eventually parted ways with manager Alex Cora. Then, everything changed.

Ahead of the 2026 MLB Playoffs, NESN released a hype video that chronicled the team's improbable journey from one of the lowest points of the season to a postseason berth.

"There was not a soul who saw this coming," the video begins.

That sentiment sets the tone for the nearly six-minute look back at a season that appeared to be slipping away before Boston found a way to turn it around.

The Red Sox opened the season with a 9-17 record, including an 0-4 mark against division opponents. The offense struggled, injuries piled up and Boston eventually fell to 18-25.

"We dug ourselves a tremendous hole," the video continues. "We got to start winning games."

The Red Sox began a remarkable winning streak, ripping off four consecutive victories, then five, six and seven. The streak reached eight, nine, 10 and eventually 15 straight games.

The turnaround came with plenty of change along the way.

Former Triple-A Worcester manager Chad Tracy took over as Boston's interim manager after Cora's departure. The Red Sox also dealt with significant injuries, including Roman Anthony 's wrist issue, Trevor Story 's groin injury and Garrett Crochet 's shoulder inflammation.

Still, the team kept going. The Red Sox made several additions, highlighted by the acquisition of catcher Adley Rutschman . The moves helped Boston continue its climb.

As key players returned and new additions made an impact, the Red Sox positioned themselves for a postseason push. They eventually clinched a playoff spot, completing a turnaround that seemed almost impossible months earlier.

The final message of the video is simple.

"You stared the impossible in the face, and you beat it back."

articles.title: World Grand Prix Darts: Luke Humphries and James Wade reach round two as Josh Rock and Chris Dobey dumped out
articles.summary: Luke Humphries - the new title favourite after Luke Littler's exit - beats below-par Dave Chisnall before appearing to shush member of crowd, will face Jermaine Wattimena next; other winners on Tuesday include Gian van Veen, Gary Anderson, Stephen Bunting and debutant Niels Zonneveld
articles.body:
Humphries - who has made the last three finals in this event, winning in 2023 ahead of two runners-up finishes since - is the new favourite to triumph this year following defending champion Luke Littler's shock defeat to Luke Woodhouse on the opening night.

Cool Hand, sporting a scab on his forehead he put down to an allergic reaction, defeated Chisnall 2-0 while averaging only 80.41 and going at 26 per cent on his doubles as he secured a second-round meeting with Chris Dobey's conqueror Jermaine Wattimena.

Chisnall had a chance to break Humphries and push for a deciding set only to bust his score, before the world No 2 wrapped up victory on double four and then appeared to shush someone in the crowd.

Dobey was one of two seeds to tumble on Tuesday evening, alongside Josh Rock, who fell to Niels Zonneveld as the Dutch debutant peeled off three ton-plus finishes in the third set to book a last-16 date with Gary Anderson.

Rock - who at one point attempted an audacious 101 finish with bullseye, one, bullseye - had lit up proceedings by following a 180 with a roof-raising 151 to break Zonneveld and ensure a deciding set.

Dobey, meanwhile, suffered a first-round exit for the third year running.

'Hollywood' - who burned four darts to break Wattimena in the opening leg - averaged below 80 and really struggled to hit the mandatory starting double in legs, with a sizzling 128 finish at the start of the second set his only moment of magic as he lost 2-0.

Wade progresses but more Grand Prix woe for Heta

James Wade fought back from a set down and shrugged off six missed match darts in the space of two visits to beat Joe Cullen 2-1 as he resumed his bid for a third Grand Prix title and first in 16 years.

A key moment came in the fourth leg of the second set when Wade hit the bull for a finish of 81, just as Cullen was eyeing a break that would have left him throwing for victory.

Wade faffed about before getting over the line, squandering arrows at double top and double 10 in the third leg of the deciding set before pinning double 10 in the next to advance.

Wade's reward is a clash with Stephen Bunting, who defeated Andrew Gilding 2-1 in the final match of the round.

There was further Grand Prix despair for Damon Heta as he suffered a sixth-straight first-round loss - the Australian has never won a match here - after surrendering a one-set lead and wasting a match dart at double five in the second set against Anderson.

Anderson, runner-up in 2016 to Michael van Gerwen, swept the third set 3-0 while averaging 110.

Gian van Veen saw off fellow Dutchman Dirk van Duijvenbode in straight sets for his first victory on this stage after round-one exits in 2024 and 2025, to Ross Smith and Littler respectively.

However, Van Duijvenbode missed two tries at double 16 to set up a decider having belatedly found his scoring form after an abject display while losing the first five legs.

Van Veen will play Ryan Searle next after 'Heavy Metal' punished four missed match darts from William O'Connor to progress as he won the final three legs of their encounter having lost the previous five.

O'Connor's electric run after losing the first set included taking out 95 with back-to-back double 19s but the Irishman - appearing at this event for the first time in over a decade - then lost his way.

articles.title: WWE NXT Results, Winners, Live Grades, Reaction, Highlights of Waller Title Match and Full Show
articles.summary: The September 29 edition of WWE NXT promised major title action as well as more Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic matches.
articles.body:
The September 29 edition of WWE NXT promised major title action as well as more Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic matches.

Emily Agard broke the news that Mason Rook would not be competing for the NXT Championship, but Grayson Waller would still defend the gold in the main event.

Zaria defended the Women's North American Championship against Thea Hail. In the continuing first round of the Dusty Classic, Fraxiom faced DarkState while BirthRight fought AAA's Mini Vikingo and Chazz "Starboy" Hall.

Check out all the results, highlights and live grades for a big night of NXT television on The CW.

Women's North American Championship: Zaria (c) vs. Thea Hail

Last Time in Action: Zaria alongside La Catalina defeated Zaria alongside Kelani Jordan (NXT, September 22).

Zaria charged at Hail to start the match, but the challenger started to find opening to stretch at the left arm of the champion.

The champion fired back with a forearm smash and clothesline on the floor to send the match to the first Picture-in-Picture break.

Back from break, Zaria blasted Hail with a Headbutt, but the challenger fired back by tossing the champion over the top rope followed by a tope suicida.

Hail followed with a Crossbody and Exploder Suplex. Zaria caught her, but Hail turned it into a Sunset Flip for a near-fall.

The challenger hit a Meteora into the ropes followed by the World's Littlest Slam and a Springboard Senton attempt. Zaria caught her into a German Suplex, only for Hail to quickly transition into a Kimura.

The champion powered her way free followed by a Spear and F5 to seal the victory.

Typically, Zaria matches build steadily, but this had a noticeably abrupt ending despite a strong stretch for much of the match.

The dynamic of Hail's arm work clashing with the overwhelming power of Zaria worked well to sell that the underdog had a chance to steal it.

However, the final few moves fell flat as they awkwardly transitioned from one signature move to the next to set up a bland finish.

Despite decent time for the action and multiple matches recently that made Hail look like a threat to Zaria, this came off as an extended squash.

Hail was treated as a speed bump for Zaria, who will now turn her full attention to Izzi Dame.

Who knows where Hail goes from here especially since it looks like her only friend in NXT, Jaida Parker, got the call-up to Raw.

Zaria def. Hail by pinfall to retain the Women's North American Championship.

NXT paid tribute to the late former NXT champion Neville.

The show started with Robert Stone telling Grayson Waller that anyone on the roster could challenge him for the NXT Championship tonight.

Stone's tone when discussing Mason Rook's injury did not sound good. Hopefully his injury is not too serious.

Hail needs a more defined character, but her dance is easy to replicate motion that could get over with bigger audiences if she is used well.

Myles Borne Tells the Fans to "Go to Hell"

Myles Borne said he was inspired by "All Ego" Ethan Page to finally realize his own potential, turning his back on everyone that did not truly know him.

He told the fans he was no longer "the underdog". He is "The Favorite". He was done being the better man surrounded by hypocrites.

He ended his speech by looking directly into the camera and telling everyone to "go to hell".

NXT is typically good about testing the talent both as faces and heels, and this next stage of Borne's career will be a massive test.

He has to show that he can be one of the top heels in NXT. He has the in-ring talent for it, but can he sell the promo work?

This was not the best first impression. While he got solid heat, he did not present any strong reason for turning, mainly stating that he was influenced by his Page feud that ended back in May.

Getting heat can also make it harder to hear him speak, which makes it harder still for him to sell his points.

NXT has massively pushed Borne in the past, so he will likely get plenty of chances to make the most of this shot.

The "What?" chants are still not gone for good, unfortunately. Those chants are especially bad when directed at a deaf man.

It is always awkward when heels tried to get lines over like "social justice warrior crap".

Backstage, Noam Dar and Romeo Moreno spoke with The Wagner Brothers and Fraxiom. The Vanity Project arrived to declare their plan to face The Wagner Brothers in the final.

Emily Agard interviewed Grayson Waller, who promised he was not afraid of anyone in NXT answering the challenge later.

Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic: BirthRight vs. Mini Vikingo and Chazz "Starboy" Hall

Last Time in Action: Channing "Stacks" Lorenzo and Uriah Connors alongside Lexis King defeated EK Prosper, Sean Legacy and Zilla Fatu (NXT, September 22). Chazz "Starboy" Hall lost to Lexis King in his NXT debut (NXT, April 7). This was the televised debut of Mini Vikingo in NXT.

The pace of the match was too fast early for BirthRight until they caught Starboy and Mini Vikingo diving outside and sent them into the steel, sending the match to commercial break.

Stacks and Connors isolated Hall for a while, but Mini Vikingo would not be stopped once he got the hot tag. He was flying around both men and kept the pace with a Starboy tag in.

BirthRight almost put away Hall with a Connors Stunner into a Stacks Elbow Drop, but Mini Vikingo broke up the pin with a springboard.

Mini Vikingo took out Connors on the floor with a springboard corkscrew then Hall hit a Tornado DDT to set up a Mini Vikingo 630 Senton on Stacks to win.

BirthRight tried to beat down the winners afterward, but Zilla Fatu arrive to send them all packing. He then declared he was going to answering Waller's NXT Championship open challenge.

Mini Vikingo and Starboy are electric high-fliers, so it was clear immediately that they needed to advance in this tournament.

Both men shined in each moment of this contest. While Stacks and Connors were outmatched by their athleticism, they played their roles well as strong bases to wild stunts.

This is not the typical WWE match as neither Starboy or Mini Vikingo shined in terms of character work or psychology.

It was simply all action, and for this moment, that was enough. The underdogs pulled off the upset and should be fun to watch as long as they stick together.

Mini Vikingo and Hall def. Stacks and Connors by pinfall to advance in the Dusty Classic.

Lizzy Rain asked Robert Stone about the next shot at Kelani Jordan. Mini Vikingo and Hall arrived, and Stone encouraged them to deliver for Rey Mysterio, who chose them for this tournament.

While Worlds Collide has not aired yet, Starboy referenced Mini Vikingo's No. 1 contender match win on the show during the backstage segment.

Charlie Dempsey at ringside was in a neck brace, which Zilla took credit for later.

In an NXT Chronicle, Cruz Montana talked about his history. He showed his pride for his mother and thanked his father for being there for him when he could.

Kelani Jordan Finds Out Her Next Challenger Will Be Determined in 20-Woman Multi-Brand Battle Royal

Kelani Jordan made clear that she was not handing out any title opportunities since she never got a handout.

Robert Stone interrupted to announce that next week The Standout would find out her next challenger in a 20-woman multi-brand battle royal.

Reina Volcan attacked Lani from behind and promised to victory in the battle royal.

Breaking the usual interruption trend in NXT, this was a decent promo spot for The Standout, who clearly established her mentality as champion.

The battle royal could be a fun way to make a fresh challenger for Lani at Halloween Havoc.

While Wren Sinclair and Kendal Grey are the biggest threats to The Standout as champion, this is the time to deliver a fresh match.

Especially with the multi-brand promise, this win could go to a returning Giulia, Women's ID champion Laynie Luck or a TNA star like Knockouts champion Xia Brookside.

When Lani made clear she was not afraid of anyone, the crowd chanted for the suspended Wren.

Stone advised that the battle royal would include women from NXT, Raw, SmackDown, AAA, EVOLVE and TNA (an increasingly rare mention in NXT).

Izzi Dame decorated Zaria's locker room with old pictures of her old school theater work. This is already not working as a story hook.

Saquon Shugars interrupted Naraku with Robert Stone. Stone announced Naraku vs. Shiloh Hill next week and Shugars vs. Tristan Angels in two weeks.

Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic: Fraxiom vs. DarkState

Last Time in Action: Fraxiom defeated Aero Star and Laredo Kid (Main Event, September 24); DarkState defeated Sean Legacy and Dorian Van Dux (NXT, September 15).

Fraxiom started strong, hitting hard and fast against their bigger opponents. However, DarkState recovered and sent the match to commercial break after a Backbreaker to Axiom.

Cutler and Griffin kept Axiom isolated through the break, but Axiom fought to tag in Frazer, who turned the tide.

Fraxiom hit a Double Missile Dropkick for a near-fall that Cutler broke up. Cutler helped turned the tide and set up Axiom for their finisher.

Frazer Dropkicked Axiom free to set up an Axiom Spanish Fly into a Phoenix Splash from Frazer to take the victory.

This was a fun tag team contest that was carried by Fraxiom. While the size of DarkState guided the story of the action, it looked like Griffin and Cutler were always following.

Because Frazer and Axiom were so clearly in control, this was about the closest NXT has gotten to making DarkState look like enhancement talent.

The result is absolutely for the best. Fraxiom vs. Noam Dar and Romeo Moreno in round two is money for NXT and could genuinely main event a future episode.

It also allows one of NXT's rising teams to get their win back and possibly set the stage to win the whole tournament.

Frazer and Axiom def. Cutler and Griffin by pinfall to advance in the Dusty Classic.

This was a rare Fraxiom match without a climactic miscommunication between Frazer and Axiom.

In an NXT Spotlight, Kendal Grey continued to talk with a counselor, talking about how wrestling was her whole life. She was not interested in hobbies or romance.

NXT Championship: Grayson Waller (c) vs. EK Prosper

Last Time in Action: EK Prosper alongside Sean Legacy and Zilla Fatu lost to BirthRight (NXT, September 22); Grayson Waller defeated Tony D'Angelo, Zilla and Cruz Montana to become the new NXT champion (NXT Heatwave, August 30).

After many declared their right to the title shot, Waller advised the first man in the ring got the shot. The locker room poured out, pushing through one another.

Zilla and Montana got close, but DarkState and BirthRight struck. EK Prosper slipped behind everyone and surprised the NXT champion when the bell rang.

He sent the champion reeling with his high-octane offense and stood tall in the ring into a commercial break.

Back from break, Prosper went for a turnbuckle-bounce Moonsault but fell onto the champion's knees, allowing him to turn the tide.

Waller focused on the throat of the challenger, including Headlocks, to affect the breathing of the high flier. It culminated in throwing him throat-first onto the metal of the top turnbuckle into the final PIP break.

Waller was back on the Headlock from the break. Prosper tried to fire back with strikes, but Waller kept answering, even crotching the challenger on the top rope.

Prosper connected on a Springboard Headscissors from Prosper followed by a Tornado DDT into a Michinoku Driver for the near-fall.

Waller Stomped Prosper into the mat for his own near-fall. The champion tried to use the announce table against Prosper, but the challenger sent him through it with a Springboard Moonsault.

Prosper hit a Diving Leg Lariat for another near-fall. The champion then caught the challenger trying to dive outside with a Forearm Smash followed by two Grayson Waller Effects for the victory.

While an open challenge allows anyone a shot at the gold, Prosper was not the most exciting option to challenge Waller in this spot.

Prosper is still in development mode and does not have the character work down yet to fight for the top prize in NXT.

Saquon Shugars and Shiloh Hill would have been nice one-off challengers with better build behind them.

However, it is hard to fault what Prosper brought in a big spot. He and Waller delivered a dramatic back-and-forth bout that more time than expected.

Prosper has never looked better, flying around with fire to test what how quick the champion could react.

The result was always going to be Waller on top, but the champion made a point to sell Prosper as an impressive threat.

NXT needs to capitalize on this performance and start selling Prosper as more than the nice guy that helps people. He needs a direction to match his in-ring fire.

Waller def. Prosper by pinfall to retain the NXT Championship.

Booker T told Vic Joseph to give Waller props for making an open challenge for his title, but this was not the champion's choice. Vic did not correct him.

Prosper's sell on Waller's Stomp out of the corner was wildly over-the-top, standing himself up on his head.

Waller admitted afterward to the camera that he was impressed, but Prosper did not have enough.

The show ended with a frustrated Zilla ranting about losing his shot and promising to make Lexis King pay for it. This did not land as a coda to the show.

When NXT falls too much into the same formula, it leads to flat shows no matter what action is on the card.

This is why it is nice to see these shows where NXT gets more creative in building dynamics over the course of the show and sells future episodes.

The promise of the NXT Championship open challenge allowed many stars to sell why they still want to be champion, even those that got sidetracked in recent weeks.

Kelani Jordan got to speak on her own without overloading the segment, and NXT set an interesting battle royal for next week.

Zaria vs. Thea Hail as well as both Dusty Classic matches were good, even though the finishes could be better.

The only real downside at the moment has been NXT's awkward overselling of Zilla Fatu, who would gain more natural support with a more natural push.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark's technical foul sparks furious rally as Fever avoid elimination against Aces
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark made WNBA playoff history with a points-assists double-double before halftime as the Indiana Fever surged past the Las Vegas Aces.
articles.body: Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark made WNBA postseason history Tuesday, becoming the first player to record a points-assists double-double before halftime of a playoff game. The Fever won 99-89 to avoid elimination Tuesday and force a deciding Game 3 on Thursday. Clark finished with 27 points, 15 assists and seven rebounds before fouling out with 2:45 remaining in the fourth quarter and the Fever leading 92-83. Clark become the first player in WNBA history to score at least 25 points and record 15 assists in a game (regular season or playoffs). Jackie Young led the Aces with 31 points. Las Vegas' A'Ja Wilson, who scored 22, received a technical foul in the fourth quarter for an interaction with a fan. Facing elimination in Game 2 against the defending champion Las Vegas Aces, Clark put on a clinic, leading a wild turnaround after a second-quarter technical foul to give Indiana a big lead at the break. Frustrated with the officiating following an apparent flop by Aces guard Mai Yamamoto amid heavy physical pressure, Clark picked up a technical foul late in the frame. Poking the bear backfired for the Aces. As the floor general, Clark channeled that fire immediately into a furious 24-6 surge, leading a Fever attack that forced eight second-quarter turnovers and outscored the Aces 30-17 in the frame to grab a 48-43 halftime lead. Clark posted 14 points and 11 assists in just 19 minutes, dishing 11 of Indiana's 13 team assists while feeding Kelsey Mitchell and Aliyah Boston for 30 first-half points in the paint. The third-year Fever sensation is following up a regular season where she earned AP Comeback Player of the Year and First Team All-WNBA honors, becoming the first player in league history to stack 800-plus points and 300-plus assists in a single campaign. articles.title: No TV, no smartphone, just a phone call: How Neeru Dhanda’s gold reached her mother
articles.summary: Nagoya/Jind: Clutching her BPL card, Sudesh Devi was walking from her one-room house towards the village PDS ration shop in Haryana’s Sangatpura on
articles.body: Nagoya/Jind: Clutching her BPL card, Sudesh Devi was walking from her one-room house towards the village PDS ration shop in Haryana’s Sangatpura on Tuesday morning when her battered keypad phone buzzed. It was an unknown number.“Neeru gold jeeti hai, Asiad mein (Neeru has won gold, at Asiad),” said the stranger.Asian Games Full Coverage | Schedule | Medal TallyShe stopped in her tracks. Fighting back the urge to jump for joy, she looked around for someone to verify the news.“We don’t have a TV or smartphone. I hadn’t been able to follow the news but knew last night that Neeru was to compete,” she told TOI later.Devi, 48, collected the ration and hurried back home in a daze.“I still couldn’t believe she won gold,” she said.In Nagoya, meanwhile, at a rain-swept, high-altitude shooting range, Neeru Dhanda was making a mother’s dream come true, becoming the first Indian woman, and the first Indian since the late Randhir Singh in 1978, to win gold in individual trap.India had won seven shooting gold medals at the last edition in Hangzhou but has endured a difficult campaign here. Neeru provided the country’s first gold in shooting at these Games, less than two weeks after she lay on a hospital bed, not even sure she would make the trip.Neeru had spent three days in a Bhopal hospital with suspected H1N1 flu while the national camp was under way in the city. On a liquid diet for five days, she could not get to the practice station for three-and-a-half weeks and arrived in Nagoya short of training, but not intent.On the eve of her gold-winning effort, you would not know she had been through all that.On Tuesday, rain landed on her hand and threatened to cause a disturbance. But Neeru stayed locked on to the target.“Aaj agar toofan bhi aa jaye, neeche nahi dekhna (Even if there is a storm, look it in the eye),” she told herself.The storm never came close to derailing her.But it was such a different story just a fortnight ago, when she was riddled with doubt and frail with illness. It was her personal coach Mansher Singh, a three-time silver winner in team trap, who kept her going. On the eve of her event, national coach Peter Wilson gave her a simple message: “Grind it out.”Grinding it out is something Neeru has done since she picked up a shotgun less than a decade ago.A journey that began by a pondHer journey started on the banks of a talaab (pond) close to their home.“My uncle took me to a pond and asked me to shoot a small sheet of tin. I also told myself, ‘Let’s see what I can do.’ I passed that test,” Neeru told TOI.Neeru was then inspired by her cousin Lakshay Sheoran, a silver winner in trap at the 2018 Asian Games.By 2019, she had packed her bags and moved to Bhopal because the Madhya Pradesh Shooting Academy offered free guns to its trainees. But before she could get her hands on one, she had to prove she could shoot.Uncle Somveer, Lakshay’s father and a former national wrestling champion, handed her an old country double-barrel gun and took her to the pond. It was almost as if the family was indulging a petulant kid. Today, they would be so happy that they gave in to her demands.“We had neither the money nor the resources for this sport. Lakshay helped arrange everything. My daughter even practised with his rifle. His family is related to us. Today, after seeing what my daughter has achieved, my heart is filled with happiness,” father Suresh said.A mother’s unwavering faithBehind her achievement lies a story of extraordinary struggle, sacrifice and a mother’s unwavering faith in her daughter. Poverty was just another battle on the way.Sudesh Devi took to selling buffalo milk to keep the shared dream alive.When TOI reached their one-room home, the proud mother was washing utensils. Eyes wide in wonder, she looked up and said, “You are telling me it is indeed gold? My Neeru has won gold?”And then she threw up her soap-streaked arms and let out a cheer.Soon, the stream of badhaais started. Villagers flocked in to celebrate ‘Jind ki beti’. Neeru’s feat is all the more remarkable considering that Sangatpura lies in the heart of ‘khap-land’.Father Suresh Dhanda, 56, said the family struggled to support her sporting career but never gave up.Sudesh Devi said she never regretted having daughters.“If God had given me another daughter, I would have welcomed her too. Today, daughters are proving that they can be at the forefront of everything. In the toughest of times, Neeru would tell me, ‘Ma, keep faith in me and ignore what the world says’,” she said.Neeru had decided to put marriage on hold because she wanted to first change her family’s circumstances.“She had promised me that she would first build a good house for the family and start her own family only after fulfilling that promise. After today’s victory, it feels as if all our dreams have come true,” she said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Everybody's ready to play: Jordan Walsh on Boston Celtics training camp
articles.summary: "When it's time to come and compete and play and be here, as you can see, everybody's here," said Walsh.
articles.body:
It is not every day when you get to compete against someone you grew up a fan of, regardless what field you work in. It can be even weirder to have them on your team, as Boston Celtics reserve wing Jordan Walsh recently related. "All these younger guys kind of grew up watching these guys play," said Walsh via CLNS Media after practice at training camp on Monday (Sep. 28) afternoon.

"It was funny," continued the Celtics forward. "The other day I was talking about how LeBron (James) got drafted the year I was born and then I got to play against him, which was crazy. And so just having moments like that, where it's like somebody you watch growing up who was like a legend in the game and now you've got to change your lens and look at him as like an opponent."

"It's a special thing, it's a gift, but it's also something you've got to, it comes with a little more respect, a little more humility to go out there and compete against them," said Walsh. Even with all this talk of playing against legends of the game, however, the Arkansas alum has his eyes on the prize, and arrived in Boston well before he had to show up.

"You don't have to be here until media day if you don't want to be," he said, relating he is not alone in his enthusiasm for the campaign ahead. "It's just a standard that everybody set for themselves; everybody has different times. I didn't get here at the same time (Paul George) did. PG didn't get here at the same time Mitchell (Robinson) did."

"Everybody has a different schedule, but the earlier you are here, usually the younger you are. The older you get, the longer summers you get. But when it's time to come and compete and play and be here, as you can see, everybody's here. Everybody's ready to play. Nobody's slacking behind, so that's what matters."

articles.title: ‘I see a man…’ A’ja Wilson on ‘unacceptable’ courtside altercation with Indiana Fever fan
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever’s Game 2 win against the Las Vegas Aces was marred by an unfortunate altercation between a fan and A’ja Wilson. She addressed it after the...
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever 's Game 2 win against the Las Vegas Aces was marred by an unfortunate altercation between a fan and A'ja Wilson. She addressed it after the game.

Facing elimination in front of their home crowd, the Indiana Fever put in an excellent performance against the Las Vegas Aces to win Game 2 99-89.

Late in the game, though, Sophie Cunningham was called for a foul which led to something unpleasant. Aces star A'ja Wilson ended up getting into a heated argument with a fan sitting courtside.

The fan was temporarily removed from their seat after the confrontation with Wilson. However, the fan was allowed to return later. After the game, Wilson explained her side of things.

A'ja Wilson says the man took steps towards her and pointed at her, leading to the exchange

Emotions tend to get heated in the playoffs, and this seems like another example of that. Wilson spoke after the game about the situation, explaining which behaviours she can no longer tolerate.

The Fever's statement suggested that there was no violation of the Fan Code of Conduct. A'ja also addressed that, and the fact that the fan was allowed back in the arena.

"I don't know if you guys know me… I try to play my game and keep it pushing," Wilson said. "But if I'm just walking, because I just got the foul and I'm chilling…

"If I see a man, come at me. Taking steps towards me and pointing at me? I don't give a d*** what you said. I don't give a d*** how you said it, your tone… That is unacceptable.

"You don't step towards me and point at me. I'm not for that s***, at all. Excuse my French. That there is unacceptable. And how he gets back in the game, because they said he didn't do anything…

"Of course he didn't. And that's fine. I apologised to my team because I got us a tech. But it's just certain things I'm just not going to allow anymore."

Wilson is one of the WNBA's most decorated superstars, among the greatest of all time. It seems she has now decided what she's willing to put up with and what she isn't. The hope will be that something like this doesn't happen again.

articles.title: Carson Kvapil to drive No. 8 O'Reilly car for JR Motorsports in 2027
articles.summary: Carson Kvapil will drive the No. 8 car for JR Motorsports during the 2027 NASCAR O'Reilly Series season.
articles.body:
Carson Kvapil will have a new number in 2027. Earlier in the month, JR Motorsports announced that Kvapil will drive the iconic No. 8 car during the 2027 NASCAR O'Reilly Series season. Kvapil will replace Sammy Smith, who announced his departure from JR Motorsports at the end of the year.

It has been an amazing stretch for the driver of the No. 1 car after winning two races. Kvapil currently sits third in the Chase standings with a 37-point deficit and seven races remaining. The JR Motorsports driver is right in the thick of the championship hunt in the O'Reilly Series.

After running a few races in the No. 9 JR Motorsports entry and DGM Racing, Kvapil will have a stable home in the No. 8 car. The JR Motorsports driver is enjoying a breakout season that isn't over yet. By the time 2027 arrives, Kvapil hopes he is an O'Reilly Series champion.

articles.title: Satellite settles down, sweeps Melbourne for 15th win this season
articles.summary: Satellite defeated Melbourne in a sweep behind another efficient offensive performance as the Scorpions won their 11th match in the last 12.
articles.body:
It was an energized environment at Melbourne High School on Sept. 29 as the Bulldogs hosted Satellite in the only meeting of the season.

After a strong start by Melbourne, Satellite settled into the match and dominated the rest of the way for a convincing sweep 25-18, 25-11, 25-7.

"It was good. It kind of went like we thought. We knew we had to take their best shot to start. They were going to be there motivated," Satellite head coach Daren Bolton said. "A lot of these girls are friends. A lot of them very familiar with each other, so we knew coming into the gym that we had to take control of the momentum and make sure that we kept it."

It was an emotional match for players on both sides squaring off against many friends. Scorpions junior Lily Sigety returned to Melbourne for the first time since transferring to Satellite after last school year.

Melbourne opened the match with an 8-3 lead when Bolton called timeout. The team responded with a 10-1 run midway through the opening set to flip a 12-9 deficit into a 19-13 lead.

The Scorpions scored the first 5 points of both sets two and three and never looked back. They finished the match with 42 kills and 11 aces.

"I think you can tell in the beginning there was a lot of emotion. I kind of expected it out of my team too. When I called the timeout, it was just to settle down," Bolton said. "Didn't tell them to do anything differently. Just take a deep breath, play the game like you know how to play the game and once we got settled in and did our game, we felt confident in our abilities."

Satellite sophomore Harper Lanza led the way with 13 kills, 2 aces and 1 block. In set one, Lanza spiked 3 consecutive kills to bring up set point. She clinched set two with a kill and a block on the final two points.

"It was really good. We played really consistent. I think I did all right," Lanza said. "Always can be better, always can improve, always can have more chemistry with the team and stuff like that but I think so far it's going pretty well."

Lanza entered the match second on the team in kills (140), second in assists (174) third in aces (24), fourth in blocks (23) and fifth in digs (119). After this match, Lanza set a new career high in kills surpassing her eighth-grade total of 147.

"I think it's been pretty good, especially in the way of connecting with my other setter and all my hitters," Lanza said. "I think it can definitely always improve, but I think it's going well."

In her first match back at Melbourne, Sigety finished with 7 kills and 4 aces. She served back-to-back aces to open the match. Sophomore Kenzie Little finished with 10 kills and 3 aces. Senior Lily Ruda spiked 7 kills.

"I think we tried to get her (Sigety) the ball as much as we could and she could make her own impression," Lanza said.

Scorpions sophomore Cady Tinch entered the match with a team-high 242 digs. Tinch, who served 2 aces on Sept. 29, will surpass her freshman digs total with three matches left in the regular season.

"The biggest thing that she (Tinch) brings is the leadership on the floor. She commands the floor," Bolton said. "You'll hear her call every ball calling out what she sees. She's not a sophomore. She plays like she's been the senior."

Satellite improved to 15-5 and it'll host Edgewood on Oct. 1 in its third match in four days. With districts two weeks away, Lanza said the team shares a belief in what they can achieve in the postseason.

"We're a very strong team and we can go against anybody. No matter the team, we can put up a fight," Lanza said. "Definitely trying to make as far as a run in the playoffs as we can and hopefully win districts."

It was a tough performance for Melbourne as it finished the night with just 17 kills and 5 aces as the Bulldogs struggled to side out against Satellite's dynamic attack.

"That was atrocious," Melbourne head coach Maira Thompson said. "Unfortunately, things come up. We had some medical issues on the team and when those players can't perform, we need other people to step up. It fell apart and it worse than I could have probably expected."

A bright spot for the Bulldogs was the play of senior Maiya Jackson. She led the team with 8 kills and 1 block.

"I think she's (Jackson) truly taking on a leadership role as a captain. One of the older ones on the team and just still showing up," Thompson said. "I think it's tough to be in her position. She's a competitor. When you try to motivate, it's hard to motivate at times and I think she's doing the best that she can."

Melbourne fell to 14-5 returns to the court on Oct. 6 at Vero Beach before ending the regular season on Oct. 8 versus Titusville. Thompson said it's time for the Bulldogs to turn up the intensity with districts rapidly approaching.

"I think we have promising moments and I think we have promising potential. I just think that sometimes we get to the end of the season and there's a little bit of feeling settled," Thompson said. "This is the time you have to turn it on. This is the most important time of the season. Unfortunately, we've shown a decrease in that excitement and that's the struggle for me."

Holy Trinity starts slow, battles back to defeat Space Coast 3-2

Holy Trinity def. Space Coast 3-2 (9-25, 26-24, 25-13, 22-25, 15-11)

After Space Coast defeated Holy Trinity in a reverse sweep on Sept. 1, the Tigers avenged that defeat with a five-set win of their own for their third-straight win overall.

Holy Trinity sophomore Stella Dawson led the team with 16 kills. Senior Brooke Ellingson and junior Elle Butera posted 15 and 11 kills, respectively, as sophomore setter Sam Smith finished with 48 assists. Tigers senior Gracin Borboroglu dug 33 balls and Ellingson finished with 24 digs to complete a double-double.

Holy Trinity played Eau Gallie on Sept. 30 with a 5-9 record. Space Coast dropped to 10-10 and it'll play at West Shore on Oct. 1.

Astronaut def. Bayside 3-0 (25-9, 25-6, 25-9)

The War Eagles won their eighth match in the last nine with a dominant sweep of Bayside. Astronaut improved to 11-8 and it'll host Titusville on Oct. 6.

The Bears faced Fort Pierce Westwood on Sept. 30 with a 5-12 record. They'll play their fourth match in four days on Oct. 1 versus Melbourne Central Catholic.

Brevard Christian def. Palm Bay 3-2 (25-27, 25-14, 22-25, 29-27, 17-15)

Palm Bay suffered its second defeat to Brevard Christian as it lost in five sets for the third time in the last two weeks. The Pirates dropped to 6-8 and they'll face Fort Pierce Westwood on Oct. 1.

Melbourne Central Catholic def. Merritt Island Christian 3-1 (25-20, 25-15, 22-25, 25-23)

The Hustlers snapped a two-match losing streak with a four-set road win over the Cougars. Melbourne Central Catholic improved to 8-9 ahead of its road match at Bayside on Oct. 1. Merritt Island Christian moved to 11-7 ahead of its Oct. 1 match at Pineapple Cove West Melbourne.

Odyssey Charter def. Pineapple Cove West Melbourne 3-1 (23-25, 25-13, 25-14, 25-19)

Odyssey Charter matched its win total from last season with its fourth straight win to move to 9-5. The Titans travel to Halifax Academy on Oct. 1. Pineapple Cove West Melbourne fell to 5-12 and it'll host Merritt Island Christian on Oct. 1.

articles.title: Sam Mayer joins JR Motorsports for 2027 NASCAR O'Reilly Series season
articles.summary: Sam Mayer will drive the No. 1 car full-time for JR Motorsports during the 2027 NASCAR O'Reilly Series season.
articles.body:
JR Motorsports today announced that Sam Mayer will be making his return to the organization for the 2027 NASCAR O'Reilly Auto Parts Series season behind the wheel of the No. 1 Chevrolet. Mayer, who will be entering his fifth year behind the wheel of a JRM Chevrolet and seventh year in the NOAPS will be accompanied by partner Starkey for the duration of the 2027 season.

"I'm looking forward to working with Sam again," said Dale Earnhardt Jr. "JRM and Sam know how to win races together and it's my belief that Sam has improved as a driver since our past relationship. I appreciate Sam's eagerness to win, and I know he's excited to get back in the building and get to work. We're also excited to welcome Starkey to the team and look forward to building a strong relationship and accomplishing great things together."

Headquartered in Eden Prairie, Minn., Starkey is a global leader in hearing technology and innovation, known for advancing AI-powered hearing solutions that help people hear more naturally and stay connected to the world around them. Starkey brings together artificial intelligence, advanced engineering and human-centered design to create hearing technology that fits seamlessly into everyday life. Through innovation and partnerships with hearing care professionals, Starkey is helping people hear better, live better and experience more of the moments that matter.

"Great partnerships have the power to change conversations, and this one gives us a platform to do exactly that," said Brandon Sawalich, President and CEO of Starkey. "Hearing health belongs in every conversation about performance, protection and quality of life. In a sport where sound is a vital part of the experience for both drivers and fans, and hearing is exposed to extreme environments, protecting it should be just as important as protecting any other part of the body. Starkey is proud to bring our leadership in hearing technology and innovation to the racing community and inspire a new generation to think differently about hearing health and conservation."

Mayer, a native of Franklin, Wis., began his NOAPS career with JRM in 2021 and found much success with the organization, earning a combined seven wins, 33 top-fives, 57 top-10s and a Championship 4 appearance in 2023. Additionally, Mayer previously raced for JRM in their vaunted Late Model program in 2018-19, which included a victory in the prestigious Bobby Isaac Memorial.

"I am really happy to be back with JR Motorsports and back behind the wheel of the No. 1 Chevrolet," said Sam Mayer. "I'm really grateful to continue my career with the organization that gave me my start and thankful to Starkey for being an incredible partner and for their continued support in my racing career. There is still some racing left to do this year and I am focused on that, but I can't wait to get the 2027 season underway at Daytona with JRM."

Additional details about the No. 1 Starkey team will be announced at a later date.
